encrier.text: The encrier prepares inks intended for handwriting or printing, mixing pigments, binders and solvents according to recipes specific to each use.

enfourneur.label: Enfourneur
enfourneur.summary: Glassworker or ceramicist who loads the kiln before firing.
enfourneur.text: The enfourneur loads the crucibles or pieces to be fired into the kiln — glassworks, pottery, bakery depending on context — an operation that determines the success of the melt or firing.

engageur.label: Engageur
engageur.summary: Recruiter responsible for organizing the departure of workers to the colonies.
engageur.text: The engageur recruits workers and settlers intended to settle in overseas territories under an indenture contract (hence the term "engagé"), an activity linked to French colonization and particularly well documented for recruitment to New France (present-day Quebec) in the 17th–18th centuries.

engagiste.label: Engagiste
engagiste.summary: Manager responsible for running an estate on behalf of its owner.
engagiste.text: The engagiste directs the complete running of a farming estate on behalf of an owner, under a lease or an indenture contract — a function close to that of the estate manager.

englobeur.label: Englobeur
englobeur.summary: Ceramics worker who loads and unloads pieces from the porcelain kiln.
englobeur.text: The englobeur takes part in porcelain firing: he loads and unloads pieces from the globe kiln, a delicate operation that determines the quality of the firing.

engraneur.label: Engraneur
engraneur.summary: Miller who regulates the mill's grain feed.
engraneur.text: The engraneur regulates the flow of grain poured into the mill's hopper, so as to ensure regular, good-quality grinding.

engraveur.label: Engraveur
engraveur.summary: Craftsman who engraves decoration and motifs onto various materials.
engraveur.text: The engraveur practises engraving on metal, wood or stone, to create decoration, reproductions and ornaments — an old spelling variant of "graveur" (engraver).

engreneur.label: Engreneur
engreneur.summary: Agricultural mechanic who operates and feeds threshing machines.
engreneur.text: The engreneur operates and feeds threshing machines at grain-threshing sites, a trade that appeared with the mechanization of agriculture in the 19th century.

enhayeur.label: Enhayeur
enhayeur.summary: Brick-works worker who organizes the stacking of bricks for drying.
enhayeur.text: The enhayeur arranges freshly moulded bricks so as to ensure their even drying before firing in the kiln.

enjoliveur.label: Enjoliveur
enjoliveur.summary: Merchant of trimmings and ornaments for clothing and headwear.
enjoliveur.text: The enjoliveur sells precious fabrics, lace, beads and other accessories intended to embellish clothing and headwear.

enlumineur.label: Enlumineur (illuminator)
enlumineur.summary: Artist who paints and decorates medieval manuscripts.
enlumineur.text: The enlumineur decorates manuscripts with illuminated initials, miniatures and painted ornaments, often in gold leaf. The trade flourished in monastic and then lay workshops of the Middle Ages, before declining with the spread of printing from the 15th century.

enlumineur_de_jouets.label: Enlumineur de Jouets
enlumineur_de_jouets.summary: Worker painting toys, particularly dolls, to give them a realistic look.
enlumineur_de_jouets.text: The enlumineur de jouets paints toys, particularly dolls, to give them a realistic look (complexion, facial features).

enoiseur.label: Énoiseur
enoiseur.summary: Worker who cracks walnuts to extract the kernels.
enoiseur.text: The énoiseur cracks walnut shells to delicately extract the kernels, a seasonal activity of walnut-producing regions. In Poitou, the synonym "échalupeur" was used, "chalupe" there denoting the walnut shell.

enoueur.label: Énoueur
enoueur.summary: Textile worker who removes knots and impurities from woollen fabrics with tweezers.
enoueur.text: The énoueur removes, using small tweezers, the knots ("énoues"), straw bits and burrs present on the surface of woollen fabrics, a finishing step meant to improve the look of the cloth before sale. Old occupational dictionaries attach to this same work many regional synonyms: "épinceteur", "épinceleur", "épincheleur", "épinceur", "époutieur", "époutilleur" and "époutisseur".

entailleur.label: Entailleur
entailleur.summary: Craftsman who cuts stone to make architectural elements.
entailleur.text: The entailleur is a regional synonym for stonecutter: he cuts stone to create architectural and decorative elements.

enterreur.label: Enterreur
enterreur.summary: Funeral-service worker responsible for burying the deceased.
enterreur.text: The enterreur digs graves and buries the deceased in the cemetery, a task generally entrusted to the gravedigger, with whom the term is often conflated.

entrepreneur.label: Entrepreneur (contractor)
entrepreneur.summary: Person who organizes and runs an economic activity or a building project at his own risk.
entrepreneur.text: The entrepreneur organizes and directs, often at his own financial risk, an economic activity or a construction project — building, public works, service provision — employing and coordinating a workforce. The term is frequently specified in records with a specialty (masonry, transport, etc.).

entrepreneur_en_maconnerie.label: Entrepreneur en maçonnerie
entrepreneur_en_maconnerie.summary: Business head who directs masonry construction sites.
entrepreneur_en_maconnerie.text: The entrepreneur en maçonnerie directs a construction site: he employs and coordinates masons, stonecutters and labourers, and answers for the work to the project owner, a status distinct from that of the simple salaried mason.

envoyeur.label: Envoyeur
envoyeur.summary: Miner who loads the carts to move ore out of the galleries.
envoyeur.text: The envoyeur loads extracted ore into mine carts and organizes its transport out of the galleries, a key post in the mining-extraction chain.

eperonnier.label: Éperonnier
eperonnier.summary: Craftsman who makes spurs, bits and other metal pieces of a horseman's equipment.
eperonnier.text: The éperonnier works metal to make spurs, bits and other harness accessories for horsemen, a craft linked to equestrian equipment and often close to that of the armourer. The old form "espronnier" is also found.

epetier.label: Épétier
epetier.summary: Craftsman who makes swords and other edged weapons.
epetier.text: The épétier forges and mounts swords and blades, a craft close to that of the sword-furbisher and the armourer.

epetisseur.label: Épetisseur
epetisseur.summary: Textile worker who removes surface irregularities from fabrics by hand.
epetisseur.text: The épetisseur manually corrects small surface defects in fabrics to obtain a perfectly even appearance. The term is a synonym of "énoveur" in old occupational dictionaries.

epeuleur.label: Épeuleur
epeuleur.summary: Textile worker who winds thread onto pirns before weaving.
epeuleur.text: The épeuleur winds thread onto "épeules" — large bobbins without a support — in order to prepare it for the weaving operation.

epicier.label: Épicier (grocer)
epicier.summary: Merchant of foodstuffs, originally mainly spices.
epicier.text: The épicier originally sold spices, precious goods imported from the East, before the term broadened to denote the merchant of various foodstuffs (sugar, coffee, preserves, cleaning products) — a sense still in use today for the neighbourhood shop.

epinglier.label: Épinglier
epinglier.text: The épinglier makes metal pins, a craft organized into a guild as early as the Middle Ages and which, in the 18th century, became a classic example of industrial division of labour (notably described by Adam Smith). The trade is found under several old spellings: "espingleur", "espinglier", "espinguier".

epistolier.label: Épistolier
epistolier.summary: Chaplain responsible for chanting the Epistle during religious services.
epistolier.text: The épistolier is a chaplain or clerk specialized in the liturgical chanting of the Epistle during Mass, a subordinate clergy function in great churches and collegiate churches.

eplucheur.label: Éplucheur
eplucheur.summary: In hat-making, a worker who removes the guard hair from beaver pelts with tweezers.
eplucheur.text: The éplucheur is, in hat-making, the worker who removes with tweezers the "jarre" — the coarse guard hair — covering beaver pelts, so as to leave only the down used for felting hats.

epontilleur.label: Épontilleur
epontilleur.summary: Worker who fulls woollen cloth to give it texture and strength.
epontilleur.text: The épontilleur (of cloth), also called fuller, runs woollen cloth through rollers to full it, that is, compress it and tighten its fibres, which gives it texture and strength.

eprouveur.label: Éprouveur
eprouveur.summary: Sworn officer responsible for checking and testing every firearm before its sale.
eprouveur.text: The sworn éprouveur tests every weapon leaving a manufactory — barrel strength, proper functioning — before issuing a proof mark or certificate of conformity attesting that it can be sold safely.

eprouveur_jure.label: Éprouveur Juré
eprouveur_jure.summary: Person responsible for checking and testing every firearm from a manufactory before certifying it for sale.
eprouveur_jure.text: The éprouveur juré checks and tests every firearm produced by a manufactory before issuing a certificate authorizing its sale.

epuiseur.label: Épuiseur
epuiseur.summary: Quarryman responsible for extracting raw stone from the quarry.
epuiseur.text: The épuiseur extracts raw stone from quarries, a quarryman's task consisting of freeing and bringing out blocks before they are cut.

epurateur.label: Épurateur
epurateur.summary: Oil-mill worker who refines oils to make them edible.
epurateur.text: The épurateur is the oil-mill worker responsible for refining raw oils (olive, rapeseed, walnut) to remove impurities and obtain a good-quality edible oil.

equarrisseur.label: Équarrisseur (knacker)
equarrisseur.summary: Worker who cuts up the carcasses of dead animals, or a craftsman who squares stone and wood.
equarrisseur.text: The équarrisseur has two main jobs: in the context of road/sanitation services, he cuts up the carcasses of dead animals to recover hides, fat and bone; in construction, he squares — that is, gives right-angled shape to — stones or roof timbers.

ermaille.label: Ermaillé
ermaille.summary: Cowherd specialized in making Gruyère cheese on alpine pastures.
ermaille.text: The ermaillé is a cowherd who, on alpine pastures, turns his herd's milk into Gruyère cheese, a trade attached to the cheesemaking tradition of the mountain regions of French-speaking Switzerland and Savoy.

ermitano.label: Ermitaño (Spanish hermitage keeper)
ermitano.summary: Person who lived beside a hermitage chapel and looked after it, often collecting alms for its upkeep.
ermitano.text: The ermitaño looked after an ermita, a chapel or shrine away from the village: he cleaned it, rang the bell, received pilgrims and collected alms for its upkeep. He usually lived in an adjoining house and was appointed by the council, the confraternity or the bishop; he was not necessarily a member of a religious order.

escaillier.label: Escaillier
escaillier.summary: Roofer who lays slates on roofs.
escaillier.text: The escaillier lays slates to cover and waterproof roofs; the word comes from "escaille", a regional term (Wallonia, northern France) denoting slate, and is also found in the spellings "escalier" and "escallier".

escamoteur.label: Escamoteur
escamoteur.summary: Fairground performer specialized in illusion and conjuring tricks.
escamoteur.text: The escamoteur entertains the public with conjuring and illusion tricks, a trade of the strolling player and fairground performer attested since the Middle Ages.

escardeur.label: Escardeur
escardeur.summary: Craftsman who makes carding combs for the textile industry.
escardeur.text: The escardeur makes carding combs, tools fitted with metal teeth used by carders to disentangle and prepare textile fibres.

escarpeur.label: Escarpeur
escarpeur.summary: Worker who clears rocks obstructing construction sites or roads.
escarpeur.text: The escarpeur extracts or clears rocks that obstruct a building plot or the route of a road, work close to that of the quarryman.

eschaudeur.label: Eschaudeur
eschaudeur.summary: Merchant of "échaudé" pastries, made of soft dough dipped in hot water.
eschaudeur.text: The eschaudeur makes and sells "échaudés", small pastries of soft dough poached in hot water before baking — a popular confectionery attested since the Middle Ages.

escholier.label: Escholier (scholar)
escholier.summary: Student of the medieval universities, particularly of law or theology.
escholier.text: The escholier (old spelling of "écolier") is the student of medieval and early modern universities, following in particular the teaching of law or theology in the great faculties (Paris, Orléans, Montpellier).

esclopier.label: Esclopier
esclopier.summary: Clog-maker making wooden shoes, a term of Occitan origin.
esclopier.text: The esclopier makes wooden clogs; the word comes from the Occitan/Provençal "esclop", denoting the clog, and remains attested as an occupational name in southern France, while elsewhere "sabotier" is used instead.

escoffier.label: Escoffier
escoffier.summary: Old Provençal term for a shoemaker.
escoffier.text: The escoffier is, in Occitan-Provençal ("escofièr"), a shoemaker — maker and repairer of shoes. This occupational name directly gave rise to the surname Escoffier, made famous by the great chef Auguste Escoffier.

escompteur.label: Escompteur
escompteur.summary: Banker who advances funds against commercial paper due at a later date.
escompteur.text: The escompteur practises discounting: he advances to a merchant the value (minus interest) of a bill of exchange or a note before it falls due, thereby easing the cash flow of trading houses.

escordasseur.label: Escordasseur
escordasseur.summary: Worker who cards wool to prepare the fibres for spinning.
escordasseur.text: The escordasseur cards wool, disentangling and aligning the fibres to prepare them for the spinning operation.

escoriateur.label: Escoriateur
escoriateur.summary: Worker who prepares hides by flaying them for tanning.
escoriateur.text: The escoriateur, a term attested in Normandy, prepares animal hides intended for the tannery by flaying, a step upstream of leatherwork.

escribano.label: Escribano (Spanish scrivener-notary)
escribano.summary: Spanish public officer who authenticated deeds, contracts and judicial or municipal acts.
escribano.text: In the Crown of Castile, the escribano gave public faith to the contracts, wills and judicial or municipal acts he drew up and kept. There were several kinds: the royal escribano, appointed by the king and entitled to act throughout the kingdom; the escribano del número, whose number was limited in each town; and the escribanos of the town council, who kept its minutes. The Notaries Act of 1862 separated extrajudicial public faith, entrusted thereafter to notaries, from judicial functions.

escripvant.label: Escripvant
escripvant.summary: Schoolmaster responsible for teaching children to write.
escripvant.text: The escripvant teaches children the art of writing, a teaching function distinct from that of the écrivain public who drafts deeds on others' behalf.

escrivao_da_camara.label: Escrivão da câmara (municipal clerk)
escrivao_da_camara.summary: Clerk of the municipal council, who recorded council meetings and kept the municipality's books.
escrivao_da_camara.text: The escrivão da câmara writes up the minutes of council meetings (vereações), registers by-laws, resolutions and notices, issues certificates and keeps the books and archive of the municipality. A central figure of municipal administration, he was often appointed for life and the office could pass from father to son. The minute books he wrote are an important source for local history.

escrivao_dos_orfaos.label: Escrivão dos órfãos (clerk of the orphans' court)
escrivao_dos_orfaos.summary: Clerk of the orphans' court, who drew up probate inventories and partitions.
escrivao_dos_orfaos.text: The escrivão dos órfãos serves alongside the judge of orphans: he draws up the records of inventory and partition of estates with minor heirs, the guardianship deeds and the guardians' accounts. The books and case files he wrote, preserved in large numbers in the district archives, provide lists of heirs, ages and property of great use for genealogy.

escuellier.label: Escuellier
escuellier.summary: Wood-turning craftsman who makes bowls, goblets and other vessels.
escuellier.text: The escuellier turns wood to make table utensils and containers — bowls, goblets, troughs and wooden casks — a common craft before metal or ceramic tableware became widespread.

esgardeur.label: Esgardeur
esgardeur.summary: Sworn official responsible for checking compliance of commercial activities, notably at Châlons-en-Champagne.
esgardeur.text: The esgardeur is a guild-sworn official responsible for overseeing the proper enforcement of trade regulations and the quality of goods, a function attested notably at Châlons-en-Champagne under the Ancien Régime.

esguillier.label: Esguillier
esguillier.summary: Craftsman who makes metal needles, an old spelling of "aiguillier".
esguillier.text: The esguillier forges and sharpens fine, sturdy needles; this is an old spelling of the needle-maker's trade.

esleu.label: Esleu
esleu.summary: Elected judge responsible, under the Ancien Régime, for tax matters.
esleu.text: The esleu ("élu") is a judicial officer, elected or holding an office, sitting in an "élection" — a jurisdiction responsible under the Ancien Régime for tax matters, notably the taille.

esmouleur_de_grandes_forces.label: Esmouleur de Grandes Forces
esmouleur_de_grandes_forces.summary: Grinder specialized in sharpening cloth-shearers' large shears.
esmouleur_de_grandes_forces.text: The esmouleur de grandes forces is a grinder specialized in sharpening the large shears ("forces") used by cloth shearers.

espadeur.label: Espadeur
espadeur.summary: Worker who beats hemp to separate the textile fibre from the woody part.
espadeur.text: The espadeur beats retted hemp stalks with the "espade", a wooden tool, to separate the tow (textile fibre) from the "chènevotte" (woody part).

espadrilleur.label: Espadrilleur
espadrilleur.summary: Craftsman who makes espadrilles with braided-rope soles.
espadrilleur.text: The espadrilleur braids the rope of the sole and mounts the canvas of espadrilles, light traditional shoes originating from southwestern France and the Pyrenees.

espilleur.label: Espilleur
espilleur.summary: Craftsman who cuts stone to make architectural elements.
espilleur.text: The espilleur cuts stone to make architectural and decorative elements, a trade close to that of the stonecutter.

espinasseur.label: Espinasseur
espinasseur.summary: Stonecutter specialized in cutting small paving stones.
espinasseur.text: The espinasseur cuts small paving stones, a specialty of the stonecutter's trade applied to paving streets and courtyards.

espoleur.label: Espoleur
espoleur.summary: Textile worker who loads bobbins for weaving brocaded patterns.
espoleur.text: The espoleur loads the "espolins" (small shuttles) used in hand-weaving to create brocaded patterns on fabrics.

esquillier.label: Esquillier
esquillier.summary: In Languedoc, a founder who casts church bells.
esquillier.text: The esquillier, a term attested in Languedoc, casts bells intended for churches, a craft requiring great mastery of bronze casting and alloying.

esquisseur.label: Esquisseur
esquisseur.summary: Draughtsman who creates the patterns for the cards used on Jacquard looms.
esquisseur.text: The esquisseur draws the motifs transferred onto the punched cards of Jacquard looms, used to weave lace and fabrics with complex patterns.

essarteur.label: Essarteur
essarteur.summary: Worker who clears wooded land to make it arable.
essarteur.text: The essarteur practises land-clearing ("essartage"): he clears and deforests land to prepare it for farming, an important activity in the great medieval land clearances.

essayeur.label: Essayeur (assayer)
essayeur.summary: Inspector responsible for checking the quality and conformity of products (precious metals, foodstuffs).
essayeur.text: The essayeur checks the quality of products — in the oldest sense, the fineness of precious metals (gold, silver) before minting or hallmarking — a technical checking role later taken up in other industries.

estaffier.label: Estaffier
estaffier.text: The estaffier is a footman who also serves as an armed bodyguard to his master.

estamier.label: Estamier
estamier.summary: Maker of estame serge, a combed-wool fabric.
estamier.text: The estamier weaves estame serge, a combed (not carded) woollen fabric that gives a smoother, sturdier cloth, used notably for undergarments.

estimateur.label: Estimateur
estimateur.summary: In the south of France, a land-surveying expert elected by a village community.
estimateur.text: In the south of France, the estimateur is a land-surveying expert elected by a village community to assess land and property.

estivandier.label: Estivandier
estivandier.summary: In southwestern France, a day-labourer hiring out his services for summer work.
estivandier.text: In southwestern France, the estivandier hires out his services for summer farm work such as harvesting, threshing and haymaking.

etaignari.label: Etaignari
etaignari.summary: At the Arc-et-Senans saltworks, a worker responsible for extinguishing the fire used to evaporate brine.
etaignari.text: At the Arc-et-Senans saltworks, the etaignari extinguishes the fire used to evaporate brine to extract salt, the final step of the heating cycle.

etaleuse.label: Étaleuse
etaleuse.summary: Cotton-mill worker spreading and winding carded cotton tow using a spreading machine.
etaleuse.text: The étaleuse works in a cotton mill where she is responsible, using a machine called a beater-spreader, for spreading and winding tow from carded cotton.

etalier.label: Étalier
etalier.summary: Itinerant merchant selling from a stall.
etalier.text: The étalier is an itinerant merchant who sells his goods from a stall, at markets or in the street.

etalonneur.label: Étalonneur
etalonneur.summary: Officer appointed to calibrate weights and measures.
etalonneur.text: The étalonneur is a public officer responsible for checking and calibrating the weights and measures used by merchants, to guarantee their conformity.

etalonnier.label: Étalonnier
etalonnier.summary: Person who, with his stallion, makes rounds of farms for stud service.
etalonnier.text: The étalonnier makes, on order, rounds of farms and breeders with his stallion, so as to have it cover mares.

etameur.label: Étameur
etameur.summary: Itinerant coppersmith who repaired household utensils.
etameur.text: The étameur is an itinerant coppersmith who repaired household utensils such as pots, pans and cauldrons, by redoing their tin coating.

etaminier.label: Étaminier
etaminier.summary: Weaver specialized in producing étamine, a light wool or silk fabric.
etaminier.text: The étaminier weaves étamine, a very light wool or silk fabric requiring great technical skill, used notably for making veils and sieving cloth.

etesteur.label: Etesteur
etesteur.summary: Aboard a cod-fishing vessel, a sailor responsible for cutting off cod heads and gutting them.
etesteur.text: The etesteur works aboard a cod-fishing vessel where he prepares cod by cutting off their heads and gutting them, before salting.

etrindellier.label: Étrindellier
etrindellier.summary: Person working with étrindelles, horsehair fabrics used in making oils and stearin.
etrindellier.text: The étrindellier works or prepares étrindelles, horsehair fabrics used in the manufacture of oils and stearin, notably for filtering.

etuviste.label: Étuviste
etuviste.text: The étuviste keeps public baths ("étuves"), establishments offering steam baths and hygiene services, common in the Middle Ages and the Renaissance.

evacuateur.label: Évacuateur
evacuateur.summary: Worker responsible for transporting and removing urban cesspit waste.
evacuateur.text: The évacuateur transports and removes town cesspit waste, a trade of urban sanitation before mains sewerage became widespread.

eventailliste.label: Éventailliste
eventailliste.text: The éventailliste makes fans, an object at once utilitarian and fashionable, particularly prized from the 17th to the 19th century.

evideur.label: Évideur
evideur.summary: Needle-making worker responsible for hollowing out the groove of a needle's eye.
evideur.text: The évideur is a specialized needle-making worker who hollows out the groove of the eye (the hole the thread passes through) on a needle.

exclaustrado.label: Exclaustrado (secularised Spanish friar)
exclaustrado.summary: Member of a religious order forced to leave his convent after the Spanish suppression of the 1830s.
exclaustrado.text: The exclaustrado was a friar or monk who had to leave his convent following the exclaustration and disentailment measures of 1835–1836, which suppressed most male convents. Many went on to serve parishes, chaplaincies or schools, or received a state pension, and they appear with this descriptor in census lists and registers.

exempt.label: Exempt
exempt.summary: Cavalry-watch officer commanding in the absence of the captain and lieutenants.
exempt.text: The exempt is a cavalry-watch officer who commands in the absence of the captain and lieutenants, carrying an ebony command staff trimmed with ivory as his badge of office.

expeditionnaire.label: Expéditionnaire
expeditionnaire.summary: Clerk responsible, in an office, for copying deeds and dispatching mail and parcels.
expeditionnaire.text: The expéditionnaire is an office clerk responsible for copying out various deeds and dispatching mail and parcels.

fabre.label: Fabre
fabre.summary: Blacksmith, from the Latin faber ("craftsman who works iron").
fabre.text: Fabre is an old term, notably Occitan, denoting the general-purpose blacksmith who works iron for domestic and agricultural needs; it comes directly from the Latin "faber", and gave rise to the surname very common in southern France (Fabre, Faure, Lefebvre depending on region being related forms).

fabricant_a_metier.label: Fabricant à métier
fabricant_a_metier.summary: Craftsman specialized in building weaving looms.
fabricant_a_metier.text: The fabricant à métier designs and builds looms, complex machines essential to the whole textile production chain, a highly skilled mechanic's craft.

fabricant_d_amadou.label: Fabricant d'amadou
fabricant_d_amadou.summary: Producer of tinder fungus prepared from a fungus for fire-lighting.
fabricant_d_amadou.text: The fabricant d'amadou prepares tinder fungus, a spongy material drawn from the fungus Fomes fomentarius, which grows on old beeches and birches, treated to become highly flammable and used with the flint striker to light fires before matches were invented.

fabricant_de_blanc.label: Fabricant de blanc
fabricant_de_blanc.summary: Wine grower who produces white wine.
fabricant_de_blanc.text: The fabricant de blanc is a wine grower specialized in producing white wine, a term denoting his specialty within the broader trade of wine grower.

fabricant_de_canons.label: Fabricant de canons
fabricant_de_canons.summary: Craftsman who makes the metal tubes of portable firearms.
fabricant_de_canons.text: The fabricant de canons is a highly specialized craftsman who forges and bores the metal tubes forming the barrels of portable firearms (rifles, pistols), a trade distinct from that of the assembler or gunsmith who fits together the complete weapon.

fabricant_de_cerceaux.label: Fabricant de cerceaux
fabricant_de_cerceaux.summary: Craftsman who produces the wooden or metal hoops used in coopering.
fabricant_de_cerceaux.text: The fabricant de cerceaux produces the hoops needed to make casks, vats and other cylindrical containers, a trade complementary to that of the cooper.

fabricant_de_creme_de_tartre.label: Fabricant de crème de tartre
fabricant_de_creme_de_tartre.summary: Craftsman who processes the tartar from wine casks to produce cream of tartar.
fabricant_de_creme_de_tartre.text: The fabricant de crème de tartre recovers the crystallized tartar that settles at the bottom of wine casks and turns it into cream of tartar, a product used in pharmacy and cooking (notably in pastry-making), a small industry linked to wine-growing regions.

fabricant_de_fides.label: Fabricant de fidés
fabricant_de_fides.summary: Savoyard craftsman who produces pasta (vermicelli) in the Italian tradition.
fabricant_de_fides.text: The fabricant de fidés produces "fidés", a kind of vermicelli, using pasta-making techniques passed down from neighbouring Italy — the word "fidé" coming from the Italian "fidelini" — a craft specialty of Savoy.

fabricant_de_galoches.label: Fabricant de galoches
fabricant_de_galoches.text: The fabricant de galoches makes galoches, shoes with a wooden sole and leather upper, lighter and more flexible than the all-wood clog, worn by working-class and rural people.

fabricant_de_gantelets.label: Fabricant de gantelets
fabricant_de_gantelets.summary: Armour craftsman who makes metal armour gauntlets.
fabricant_de_gantelets.text: The fabricant de gantelets is an armour craftsman specialized in making gauntlets, armour pieces protecting a combatant's hand and forearm.

fabricant_de_gants.label: Fabricant de gants
fabricant_de_gants.summary: Craftsman who makes gloves of leather or other materials.
fabricant_de_gants.text: The fabricant de gants makes gloves of leather, cloth or knit, a craft organized into a glovers' guild in several French towns, including Grenoble and Millau, renowned for their glove-making.

fabricant_de_jarasses.label: Fabricant de jarasses
fabricant_de_jarasses.summary: Wheelwright craftsman who builds carts and rural transport vehicles.
fabricant_de_jarasses.text: The fabricant de jarasses builds carts and rural transport vehicles, an activity falling under the wheelwright's trade.

fabricant_de_moules_a_boutons.label: Fabricant de moules à boutons
fabricant_de_moules_a_boutons.summary: Craftsman who shapes in wood the forms used as a base for covered buttons.
fabricant_de_moules_a_boutons.text: The fabricant de moules à boutons shapes small button-shaped pieces in wood, which are then used as a base by passementerie makers or goldsmiths to create buttons covered in gold thread or other precious materials.

fabricant_de_neige.label: Fabricant de neige
fabricant_de_neige.summary: Lace maker who produces a simple popular lace called "neige" (snow).
fabricant_de_neige.text: The fabricant de neige (most often a lace maker) produces a popular lace called "neige", a simple, inexpensive piece intended for the middle and working classes, as opposed to the fine, costly laces of the great lace-making centres.

fabricant_de_pannes.label: Fabricant de pannes
fabricant_de_pannes.summary: Tile-maker who produces interlocking roof tiles known as "pannes".
fabricant_de_pannes.text: The fabricant de pannes produces "panne" tiles, interlocking roof tiles, an essential element of traditional construction in many French regions.

fabricant_de_peaux_bronzees.label: Fabricant de peaux bronzées
fabricant_de_peaux_bronzees.summary: Currier specialized in a fine black leather used for mourning shoes and gloves.
fabricant_de_peaux_bronzees.text: The fabricant de peaux bronzées is a highly specialized currier who treats goat and sheep skins to produce a fine-grained black leather with a velvety finish, intended mainly for mourning shoes and gloves.

fabricant_de_pignols.label: Fabricant de pignols
fabricant_de_pignols.summary: Breton craftsman who makes scarecrow-weathervanes to protect crops.
fabricant_de_pignols.text: The fabricant de pignols creates scarecrow-weathervanes intended to frighten birds and protect crops, a rural craft attested in Brittany.

fabricant_de_ros.label: Fabricant de ros
fabricant_de_ros.summary: Craftsman who weaves fine basketware from local plant materials.
fabricant_de_ros.text: The fabricant de ros makes woven or fine basketwork objects from local plant materials, for utilitarian or decorative uses.

fabricant_de_rouge.label: Fabricant de rouge
fabricant_de_rouge.summary: Craftsman who produces lip rouge or red face powder.
fabricant_de_rouge.text: The fabricant de rouge produces a red face powder for makeup, a small cosmetics industry tied to the beauty fashions of its time.

fabricant_de_tarares.label: Fabricant de tarares
fabricant_de_tarares.summary: Craftsman who builds tarares, grain-winnowing machines.
fabricant_de_tarares.text: The fabricant de tarares builds tarares, winnowing machines that separate grain from chaff and impurities using a current of air, farm equipment that appeared in the 18th century combining precision joinery with knowledge of agricultural needs.

fabricant_en_frot.label: Fabricant en frot
fabricant_en_frot.summary: Weaver who produces coarse woollen fabrics for monastic clothing.
fabricant_en_frot.text: The fabricant en frot weaves coarse woollen fabrics, intended mainly for the clothing of monastic communities.

fabriceur.label: Fabriceur
fabriceur.summary: Layman administering the property and finances of a parish (vestryman).
fabriceur.text: The fabriceur (or fabricien, fabricier) is an elected or appointed layman who sits on the vestry board, responsible for administering the temporal property, income and material upkeep of a parish — the "fabrique" denoting this parish patrimony. The term is also found in the forms "fabriqueur" and "fabrisseur".

fabriquant_d_aiguilles.label: Fabriquant d'aiguilles
fabriquant_d_aiguilles.summary: Craftsman who makes metal sewing needles.
fabriquant_d_aiguilles.text: The fabriquant d'aiguilles forges, draws out and polishes metal needles intended for sewing. The town of L'Aigle, in the Orne, is a historic centre of French needle-making since the 15th century, an activity that long structured the local economy.

faconneur.label: Façonneur
faconneur.summary: Comb-making craftsman who thins and shapes the comb before the teeth are cut.
faconneur.text: The façonneur takes part in the comb industry after the trimmer: he thins the comb (of horn, bone or ivory) on the side where the teeth will be cut, an intermediate manufacturing step.

faconnier_de_lattes.label: Façonnier de lattes
faconnier_de_lattes.summary: Worker who prepares and lays roofing laths to order on building sites.
faconnier_de_lattes.text: The façonnier de lattes works roofing timber, going to building sites to prepare and lay the laths needed for roof coverings and structures.

facteur.label: Facteur
facteur.summary: Commercial intermediary, or craftsman who makes and repairs musical instruments.
facteur.text: The word facteur denotes, depending on context, either a commercial intermediary responsible for trading on others' behalf (grain factor, timber factor...), or a technician who makes, tunes and repairs musical instruments (piano maker, organ builder); the later modern sense of postal carrier also derives from it.

facteur_d_orgues.label: Facteur d'orgues
facteur_d_orgues.summary: Craftsman who builds, maintains and repairs pipe organs.
facteur_d_orgues.text: The facteur d'orgues designs, builds, maintains and repairs pipe organs, an art trade combining joinery, metalwork and thorough knowledge of acoustics, indispensable to equipping churches since the Middle Ages.

facteur_de_bois.label: Facteur de bois
facteur_de_bois.summary: Merchant who buys standing timber lots and resells the exploited wood.
facteur_de_bois.text: The facteur de bois buys standing forest lots and then resells the timber once felled, a commercial intermediary of the timber trade.

facteur_de_clous.label: Facteur de clous
facteur_de_clous.summary: Commercial intermediary who supplies nailmakers and markets their output.
facteur_de_clous.text: The facteur de clous links nailmakers, whom he supplies with raw materials, to the market, where he sells their nail output.

facteur_de_fabrique.label: Facteur de fabrique
facteur_de_fabrique.summary: Sales representative who sells a manufactory's products.
facteur_de_fabrique.text: The facteur de fabrique promotes and sells a manufactory's products, a sales-representative role.

facteur_de_grains.label: Facteur de grains
facteur_de_grains.summary: Merchant who buys, stores and resells grain.
facteur_de_grains.text: The facteur de grains trades in buying, storing and reselling grain, an essential intermediary between farm producers and markets.

facteur_numeraire.label: Facteur numéraire
facteur_numeraire.summary: Junior postal agent responsible for standing in for regular postmen.
facteur_numeraire.text: The facteur numéraire is a junior postal agent, responsible for standing in for regular postmen during their absences and reinforcing mail delivery.

facteur_tubiste.label: Facteur tubiste
facteur_tubiste.summary: Postal agent responsible for operating the pneumatic-post network.
facteur_tubiste.text: The facteur tubiste operates the urban pneumatic-post network, ensuring fast mail transport through pressurized tubes, a system used notably in Paris into the 20th century.

fagoteur.label: Fagoteur
fagoteur.summary: Forest worker who bundles firewood into faggots.
fagoteur.text: The fagoteur gathers and binds branches and small wood into faggots intended for domestic heating, a seasonal forest trade.

faiencier.label: Faïencier
faiencier.summary: Potter specialized in producing glazed faience.
faiencier.text: The faïencier makes faience, a porous-bodied ceramic covered with an often-painted opaque glaze, combining technical mastery with artistic sense. France had several great faience centres, including Nevers, Rouen and Moustiers, each recognizable by its characteristic decoration.

faiseur_d_arbaletes.label: Faiseur d'arbalètes
faiseur_d_arbaletes.text: The faiseur d'arbalètes combines woodwork, metalwork and cordage to make crossbows, precision weapons used in war and then for hunting and target shooting; the term also appears in the old spelling "faiseur d'aubaleste".

faiseur_d_avant_clous.label: Faiseur d'Avant-Clous
faiseur_d_avant_clous.summary: Maker of gimlets and drilling instruments used in coopering.
faiseur_d_avant_clous.text: The faiseur d'avant-clous makes gimlets and drilling instruments used in coopering; the "avant-clou" is a small gimlet used to bore wood before a nail is driven in.

faiseur_d_eau.label: Faiseur d'Eau
faiseur_d_eau.summary: At the royal court, a servant responsible for preparing drinks.
faiseur_d_eau.text: At the royal court, the faiseur d'eau is a servant responsible for preparing the drinks served at the royal table.

faiseur_d_espagnolette.label: Faiseur d'Espagnolette
faiseur_d_espagnolette.summary: Cloth-maker producing droguet or ratine, fabrics used for linings.
faiseur_d_espagnolette.text: The faiseur d'espagnolette is a cloth-maker producing droguet or ratine, fabrics made notably at Rouen, Beauvais, Reims and Châlons, used for clothing linings.

faiseur_d_esteufs.label: Faiseur d'esteufs
faiseur_d_esteufs.summary: Craftsman who makes the balls used in real tennis.
faiseur_d_esteufs.text: The faiseur d'esteufs makes "esteufs", the balls of real tennis (jeu de paume), combining different materials (leather, tow, wool) to obtain projectiles with the characteristics suited to the game.

faiseur_d_estoeuf.label: Faiseur d'Estoeuf
faiseur_d_estoeuf.summary: Maker of estoeufs, balls used in real tennis.
faiseur_d_estoeuf.text: The faiseur d'estoeuf makes estoeufs, padded balls used in real tennis (jeu de paume), the forerunner of tennis.

faiseur_d_instruments.label: Faiseur d'Instruments
faiseur_d_instruments.text: The faiseur d'instruments makes musical instruments, a generic term used before specialization into instrument maker, organ builder, etc.

faiseur_d_instruments_de_mathematiques.label: Faiseur d'Instruments de Mathématiques
faiseur_d_instruments_de_mathematiques.summary: Maker of scientific instruments: compasses, graphometers, dials, astrolabes, globes.
faiseur_d_instruments_de_mathematiques.text: The faiseur d'instruments de mathématiques makes precision scientific instruments: cross-staffs (Jacob's staffs), compasses, graphometers, dials, astrolabes, globes and other observation and measuring instruments.

faiseur_de_bas.label: Faiseur de bas
faiseur_de_bas.summary: Hosier specialized in making knitted silk stockings.
faiseur_de_bas.text: The faiseur de bas is a hosier specialized in making silk stockings, mastering the delicate techniques of luxury knitting for refined clothing items.

faiseur_de_bois_a_galoches.label: Faiseur de bois à galoches
faiseur_de_bois_a_galoches.summary: Forestry specialist who selects and prepares wood intended for galoches.
faiseur_de_bois_a_galoches.text: The faiseur de bois à galoches selects, harvests and prepares wood species suited to making clogs and galoches, a forest trade upstream of the clog-maker's work.

faiseur_de_burat.label: Faiseur de burat
faiseur_de_burat.summary: Weaver making burat, a coarse, inexpensive woollen fabric (sometimes mixed with linen), intended for the common people.
faiseur_de_burat.text: Burat is a coarse, inexpensive fabric, woven of wool or a wool-linen blend, worn by peasants and people of modest condition under the Ancien Régime. The faiseur de burat is the weaver specialized in its production, to be distinguished from weavers of fine cloth reserved for the wealthy. The term appears in notarial and parish records of several French regions, notably Auvergne and Burgundy.

faiseur_de_cadrans.label: Faiseur de cadrans
faiseur_de_cadrans.summary: Craftsman making sundials, at the crossroads of clockmaking, astronomy and engraved stone or metal.
faiseur_de_cadrans.text: The faiseur de cadrans designs and engraves sundials, on stone, metal or wood, calculating the gnomon's tilt according to the latitude of the installation site. This skill blends astronomical and mathematical knowledge with meticulous engraving or carving work. The term is found in old records before portable mechanical clockwork became widespread.

faiseur_de_cercles.label: Faiseur de cercles
faiseur_de_cercles.summary: Craftsman making the hoops (split wood or iron) that encircle and hold cask staves.
faiseur_de_cercles.text: The faiseur de cercles produces the hoops of split wood (hazel, chestnut) or iron that encircle a cask's staves and ensure its watertightness and strength. This work supplements that of the cooper proper, who assembles the staves, and in some respects overlaps with the hoop-wood cutter's trade in regions producing hoop wood.

faiseur_de_cordes_a_boyaux.label: Faiseur de cordes à boyaux
faiseur_de_cordes_a_boyaux.summary: Craftsman turning animal gut (mainly sheep) into cords for musical instruments and rackets.
faiseur_de_cordes_a_boyaux.text: The faiseur de cordes à boyaux, or gut-cord maker, prepares animal gut — most often sheep's — by cleaning, degreasing and then twisting it, to make cords used in instrument-making and for real-tennis rackets. This foul-smelling, technical work was often practised on the outskirts of towns, near slaughterhouses.

faiseur_de_faillard.label: Faiseur de faillard
faiseur_de_faillard.summary: Craftsman who shapes tool handles from beech ("faillard") wood, a regional name for beech in the Massif Central.
faiseur_de_faillard.text: "Faillard" is a regional name for beech (Fagus sylvatica), notably attested in Auvergne, alongside other variants such as "fayard" or "foutau". The faiseur de faillard cuts this hard, sturdy wood to shape farm-tool handles — forks, rakes — prized for their durability.

faiseur_de_galons.label: Faiseur de galons
faiseur_de_galons.summary: Weaver specialized in producing military braid, narrow decorated ribbons used as rank insignia.
faiseur_de_galons.text: The faiseur de galons weaves braid intended for military uniforms, narrow bands often enhanced with metal thread whose number and arrangement indicated the wearer's rank. This fine passementerie work developed particularly with the codification of uniforms from the 17th century.

faiseur_de_licts.label: Faiseur de licts
faiseur_de_licts.summary: Craftsman who makes bedding items — mattresses, bolsters, coverlets — for furnishing bedrooms.
faiseur_de_licts.text: The faiseur de licts ("lits", beds) makes the bedding elements of a bedroom: wool or feather mattresses, bolsters, coverlets, at a time when the bed was often the most costly piece of furniture in a household, sometimes even listed in detail in post-mortem inventories.

faiseur_de_padoux.label: Faiseur de padoux
faiseur_de_padoux.summary: Ribbon-maker producing padou, a coarse thread or silk ribbon used to trim and reinforce garments.
faiseur_de_padoux.text: The faiseur de padoux weaves padou, a sturdy ribbon, often of coarse thread or silk tow, used to reinforce hems, waistbands or straps rather than for purely decorative use. Cheaper than fine silk ribbon, it was used mainly for popular clothing.

faiseur_de_paisseaux.label: Faiseur de paisseaux
faiseur_de_paisseaux.summary: Forest craftsman who cuts paisseaux (vine stakes), wooden posts intended to support vine plants.
faiseur_de_paisseaux.text: The faiseur de paisseaux selects and splits wooden poles, often of chestnut, to make paisseaux — a regional name for vine stakes — planted at the foot of each vine to support it before wire trellising became widespread.

faiseur_de_peigne.label: Faiseur de peigne
faiseur_de_peigne.summary: Craftsman making combs of horn, boxwood, ivory or bone, sometimes including the fine cutting of the teeth.
faiseur_de_peigne.text: The faiseur de peigne (or peignier) shapes combs from horn, boxwood, bone or ivory, materials worked with saw and file to obtain even teeth. Some craftsmen, sometimes called "faiseurs de dents", specialized solely in cutting the teeth of an already rough-shaped comb, a division of labour common in comb-making centres such as Oyonnax.

faiseur_de_rouleaux.label: Faiseur de rouleaux
faiseur_de_rouleaux.summary: Textile worker who winds and packages ribbons onto rolls before sale.
faiseur_de_rouleaux.text: The faiseur de rouleaux works at the end of the ribbon production chain: he winds them onto calibrated spindles or rolls, according to the lengths and presentations expected by the trade, before shipping. This packaging work is found notably in ribbon-making centres such as Saint-Étienne.

faiseur_de_tour_de_geai.label: Faiseur de tour de geai
faiseur_de_tour_de_geai.summary: Itinerant showman presenting jays trained to mimic speech and perform small tricks.
faiseur_de_tour_de_geai.text: The faiseur de tour de geai is an itinerant trainer who exploits the jay's mimicry talents — a bird reputed able to reproduce sounds and words — to give small street shows. This kind of animal showman, close to bear or marmot trainers, belongs to the 18th–19th-century fairground tradition.

faiseur_de_vaisseaux_vissoire.label: Faiseur de vaisseaux vissoire
faiseur_de_vaisseaux_vissoire.summary: Cooper-carpenter building screw presses used to extract grape juice.
faiseur_de_vaisseaux_vissoire.text: The faiseur de vaisseaux à vis (or vissoire) builds the large wooden screw presses used to press grapes or fruit, assembling the screw, the plate and the solid-wood cage. This work falls at once under coopering and carpentry, and is found in wine-growing regions.

faiseuse_d_aumonieres_sarrazinoises.label: Faiseuse d'aumônières sarrazinoises
faiseuse_d_aumonieres_sarrazinoises.summary: Medieval craftswoman making "sarrazinoise" alms-purses, decorative purses of Oriental inspiration.
faiseuse_d_aumonieres_sarrazinoises.text: The faiseuses (or fesseresses) d'aumônières sarrazinoises form one of the female guilds listed in Étienne Boileau's Book of Trades (Paris, 13th century). They made alms-purses — small purses worn at the belt for money or devotional objects — adorned in a style called "sarrazinois", that is, evoking fabrics and embroidery from the East. The term "fesseresse", an old feminine of "faiseur", gradually gave way to "faiseuse".

faiseuse_de_modes.label: Faiseuse de modes
faiseuse_de_modes.summary: Dressmaker-milliner creating clothes and especially headwear in the latest fashion for a wealthy clientele.
faiseuse_de_modes.text: The faiseuse de modes, forerunner of the milliner, designs hats, headwear and sometimes outfits following fashionable trends, for a bourgeois or aristocratic clientele. The trade boomed in the 18th century, driven notably by figures such as Rose Bertin, Marie-Antoinette's fashion merchant.

falot.label: Falot
falot.summary: Carrier of a falot (large lantern) hired to light and escort passers-by in dark streets.
falot.text: "Falot" originally denotes a large portable lantern used to light one's way at night; by extension, the term denoted the lantern-carrier, a man paid to escort and light passers-by in the unpaved, unlit streets of Ancien Régime towns. This function gradually disappeared as public lighting became widespread in the 18th–19th centuries. The word "fanal", which also denotes a lantern (notably a naval or lighthouse one), is sometimes used as a synonym in records.

familiar_del_santo_oficio.label: Familiar del Santo Oficio (lay agent of the Spanish Inquisition)
familiar_del_santo_oficio.summary: Layman in the service of the Spanish Inquisition, who enjoyed privileges and had to prove "purity of blood".
familiar_del_santo_oficio.text: The familiar was a lay collaborator of the tribunals of the Inquisition, accompanying its commissioners, carrying out arrests and performing various services. Appointment required an inquiry into the candidate's "purity of blood" and conferred privileges such as a separate jurisdiction and the right to bear arms, which made it highly sought after as a mark of respectability. The position disappeared with the final abolition of the Inquisition in 1834.

familiar_do_santo_oficio.label: Familiar do Santo Ofício (lay agent of the Inquisition)
familiar_do_santo_oficio.summary: Layman in the service of the Portuguese Inquisition, who took part in arrests, summonses and other tasks.
familiar_do_santo_oficio.text: The familiar do Santo Ofício is a lay collaborator of the Portuguese Inquisition (1536-1821), responsible for assisting it in arrests, summonses, surveillance and other tasks. The title, much sought after for the prestige and privileges it conferred, required a qualification process (habilitação) that investigated the ancestry of the candidate and his wife to prove "purity of blood". These qualification files, kept in the National Archives, contain detailed genealogies and are valuable sources.

faneur.label: Faneur (haymaker)
faneur.summary: Farm worker who turns and spreads mown grass to dry it into hay.
faneur.text: The faneur takes over after mowing: using a fork and, later, a mechanical tedder, he turns and spreads the cut grass to speed its drying in sun and wind. This seasonal work, often done in groups during the June–July haymaking season, determines the quality of the hay intended to feed livestock through the winter.

fannelier.label: Feinier
fannelier.summary: Merchant of hay and fodder, supplying livestock breeders with animal feed.
fannelier.text: The feinier (or fenier, fannelier depending on region) buys hay from farmers, stores it and then resells it to breeders and horse owners, notably in town where few residents can mow their own fodder. The word comes from Old French "fein"/"fain", a variant of "foin" (hay). This trade was particularly active near market halls and post relays, where many horses were fed daily.

fargier.label: Fargier
fargier.summary: Blacksmith, a dialectal term (Occitan, Franche-Comté) derived from "fargue"/"farga", the forge.
fargier.text: Fargier is a regional variant of "forgeron", attested notably in Franche-Comté and Occitan-speaking areas, where the word comes from "farga" (the forge, in Occitan and Catalan). It denotes the craftsman who works iron at the fire and anvil to make or repair tools, ironwork and farm parts.

farinier.label: Farinier
farinier.summary: Miller or flour merchant, handling the milling or sale of processed grain.
farinier.text: The farinier can denote either the miller who turns grain into flour at the mill, or the merchant who buys flour to resell it to bakers and individuals. The term thus covers both a processing activity and a trading activity depending on place and period.

fassari.label: Fassari
fassari.summary: Worker at the royal saltworks of Arc-et-Senans responsible for shaping salt paste into loaves.
fassari.text: The fassari worked at the royal saltworks of Arc-et-Senans (Doubs), built by Claude-Nicolas Ledoux in the 18th century, where he moulded and shaped into loaves the salt paste obtained by evaporating brine — a task distinct from that of the métari, who kneaded this paste. The term illustrates the highly hierarchical organization of work in the great saltworks of the Ancien Régime.

fattore.label: Fattore (Italian estate steward)
fattore.summary: Steward who managed an estate (fattoria) for its owner and supervised the farms held by sharecroppers.
fattore.text: In central Italy, and especially in Tuscany, the fattore managed the fattoria, a group of farms entrusted to sharecropping families: he supervised the crops, kept the accounts with the tenants, sold the produce and represented the owner. He usually lived at the estate's main house and was sometimes assisted by an under-steward.

faucheur.label: Faucheur (mower)
faucheur.summary: Farm worker cutting grain or grass with a scythe, a key technical gesture of the harvest.
faucheur.text: The faucheur wields the scythe to cut grain or grass before the era of the mechanical harvester, a gesture requiring strength and coordination to achieve an even cut. Teams of mowers, often itinerant, hired themselves out from farm to farm to the rhythm of the harvests, followed by the haymakers and gleaners.

fauconnier.label: Fauconnier (falconer)
fauconnier.summary: Trainer and keeper of falcons used for falconry hunting.
fauconnier.text: The fauconnier raises, trains and cares for birds of prey (falcons, goshawks, sparrowhawks) used for falconry, an aristocratic practice much prized from the Middle Ages to the 17th century. Some great noble and royal households maintained a falconry with its own hierarchical staff, from the grand falconer down to simple assistants.

faudeur.label: Faudeur
faudeur.summary: Textile worker who folds pieces of cloth according to trade custom before sale.
faudeur.text: The faudeur takes over at the end of making a piece of cloth or fabric: he folds it into standardized formats, an operation that eases transport, storage and shop display. This post falls under the final quality control in Ancien Régime textile manufactories.

fauldeur.label: Fauldeur
fauldeur.summary: Charcoal burner, a term mainly used in Belgium and francophone northern regions for the charcoal maker.
fauldeur.text: The fauldeur practises the same trade as the charbonnier: he builds wood stacks covered with earth and moss, which he lets slowly smoulder under constant watch for several days to produce charcoal. The term, derived from "faulde" (the stack itself), is mainly attested in Wallonia and northern France.

faure.label: Faure
faure.summary: Blacksmith, an Occitan term (from the Latin "faber") very common in records of southern France.
faure.text: Faure is the Occitan form of "forgeron" (blacksmith), derived directly from the Latin "faber" (craftsman, smith). Extremely common as an occupational name and later as a surname in the langue d'oc regions, it gave rise to many family names (Faure, Lefaure, Fabre, Favre depending on region).

faux_saunier.label: Faux saunier (salt smuggler)
faux_saunier.summary: Salt smuggler, who buys or sells salt outside the taxed channels of the royal gabelle.
faux_saunier.text: The faux saunier evades the royal salt tax, the gabelle, by sourcing salt in less-taxed provinces (such as exempt Brittany) to sell it clandestinely in heavily taxed regions. The suppression of this smuggling, very active from the 16th to the 18th century, filled the galleys and prisons, and salt smuggling remains one of the great hotbeds of popular revolt under the Ancien Régime.

fayancier.label: Fayancier
fayancier.summary: Maker of faience, glaze-decorated pottery fired using techniques from Italy and then Delft.
fayancier.text: The fayancier makes faience, a porous-bodied ceramic covered with an opaque tin glaze allowing decorative painting, a technique introduced into France in the 16th–17th centuries from Italy (Faenza, which gives faience its name) and then spread via Dutch Delft models. Centres such as Nevers, Rouen, Moustiers or Quimper made it a renowned regional specialty.

feculier.label: Féculier
feculier.summary: Maker of starch extracted from potatoes or other starch-rich plants.
feculier.text: The féculier runs a starch mill, a workshop where potatoes (or other starchy plants such as cassava or wheat) are grated and then washed to extract starch by settling. This food-processing industry developed in the 19th century, notably in northern France, supplying starch for food, textiles (sizing) and papermaking.

feitor.label: Feitor (steward, overseer or factor)
feitor.summary: Manager of an estate, household or business on behalf of its owner; also the Crown's agent at an overseas trading post.
feitor.text: The feitor runs a farm, estate or household on behalf of its owner: he directs the workers, oversees crops and livestock, collects rents and renders accounts. Since the Middle Ages the term has also denoted the commercial agent of a merchant or of the Crown, notably the head of a feitoria, a Portuguese trading post abroad or overseas. In records, the context must therefore be taken into account.

femme_de_chambre.label: Femme de chambre (chambermaid)
femme_de_chambre.summary: Domestic attached to the personal service of a lady of the house: her toilette, dress, and bedroom upkeep.
femme_de_chambre.text: The femme de chambre handles the intimate service of a lady of the house — helping with grooming and dressing, caring for her personal linen and bedroom — a status closer to the mistress of the house than a mere housekeeping servant. In great households, she could supervise other female domestics.

femme_de_menage.label: Femme de ménage (charwoman)
femme_de_menage.summary: Domestic employee responsible for a home's general upkeep, housework and household cleanliness.
femme_de_menage.text: The femme de ménage cleans and maintains a home, unlike the chambermaid, who is attached to a lady's personal service. The term, still in use today, already denoted, under the Ancien Régime and in the 19th century, a domestic sometimes coming only by the day, unlike live-in staff.

femme_jure.label: Femme jurée
femme_jure.summary: Midwife examined and sworn in by the authorities, authorized to legally perform deliveries.
femme_jure.text: The femme jurée (or sworn midwife) has taken an oath before the ecclesiastical or municipal authorities after examination of her skills, which authorizes her to practise legally, including baptizing an infant in danger of death. This status, regulated from the 17th century, distinguishes the recognized midwife from the simple untrained matron.

fendeur.label: Fendeur
fendeur.summary: Slate-quarry worker who splits the slate block into thin, even sheets intended for roofing.
fendeur.text: The fendeur works in a slate quarry: using a chisel and mallet, he divides the raw slate block along its natural cleavage plane to produce thin, sized sheets, an operation requiring a very sure hand so as not to break the stone. This trade remains central in slate-quarry basins such as those of Anjou or the Ardennes.

fendeur_d_echalas.label: Fendeur d'échalas
fendeur_d_echalas.summary: Forest craftsman who splits wood into stakes (échalas) intended to support vine plants.
fendeur_d_echalas.text: The fendeur d'échalas turns wooden poles — most often chestnut, prized for its resistance to moisture — into pointed stakes intended to support vines. This work, done in the forest or a coppice workshop, was essential in wine-growing regions before wire trellising became widespread.

fendeur_de_lattes.label: Fendeur de lattes
fendeur_de_lattes.summary: Craftsman who splits wood into thin roofing laths, used notably for roofs and lath work.
fendeur_de_lattes.text: The fendeur de lattes (or fendeur lattier) cuts wood into thin, even laths by splitting rather than sawing, a technique that follows the grain of the wood and gives it better strength. These laths were used for roof framing, the lathing of thatched or tiled roofs, and trellising.

fendeur_de_merrains.label: Fendeur de merrains
fendeur_de_merrains.summary: Forest craftsman who splits oak logs into merrains, boards intended for coopering.
fendeur_de_merrains.text: The fendeur de merrains selects and splits oak into thick boards called merrains, following the grain of the wood rather than sawing it, in order to preserve its impermeability — a quality essential for the staves of casks intended for wine and spirits. This forest trade fed directly into coopering and long characterized certain state forests such as Tronçais.

fenetrier.label: Fenêtrier
fenetrier.summary: Craftsman making windows, combining wood, glass and sometimes metal work.
fenetrier.text: The fenêtrier builds window frames and, depending on the period, also glazes them, at the crossroads of joinery and glazing. Before the modern specialization of building trades, this term covered a versatile skill needed to close the openings of dwellings.

feodiste.label: Féodiste
feodiste.summary: Lawyer specialized in feudal law, responsible notably for reconstituting seigneurial land registers.
feodiste.text: The féodiste (or feudiste) is a lawyer specialized in the study of feudal law and seigneurial rights, hired by lords to revise and reconstitute the "terriers" — registers recording the rights, dues and levies owed on a piece of land. His activity intensified at the end of the Ancien Régime, a period of "seigneurial reaction" when lords sought to enforce rights that had fallen into disuse, which made féodistes particularly unpopular on the eve of the Revolution.

ferblantier.label: Ferblantier (tinsmith)
ferblantier.summary: Craftsman making and repairing tin-plate objects: kitchen utensils, boxes, lanterns.
ferblantier.text: The ferblantier works tin-plate — a thin sheet of tinned iron, thus protected from rust — which he cuts, bends and solders to make kitchen utensils, boxes, funnels, lanterns or toys. Less costly than goldsmithing or coppersmithing, this craft became widespread from the 17th century and survives today in certain regions (notably Brittany). "Ferblanquier" is an old spelling variant.

fermailler.label: Fermailler
fermailler.summary: Craftsman specialized in making clasps, hooks and small metal fastening objects.
fermailler.text: The fermailler shapes clasps and hooks, often of brass or precious metal, used to fasten clothing, belts, books or purses. This small-goldsmith or coppersmith work overlaps with that of the button-maker and the goldsmith depending on the richness of the materials used.

fermier.label: Fermier
fermier.summary: Farmer who works land in exchange for paying rent to the owner.
fermier.text: The fermier farms land he does not own, in exchange for a fixed rent ("fermage") paid to the owner, unlike the sharecropper, who shares the harvest. This status, more favourable to the tenant since independent of harvest fluctuations, spread mainly in the north and the Paris basin, while sharecropping dominated in the south and centre of France.

fermier_general.label: Fermier général (farmer-general)
fermier_general.summary: Private financier who advances tax to the king and reimburses himself by collecting indirect taxes himself.
fermier_general.text: The fermier général belongs to the Ferme générale, a company of financiers who leased from the king the collection of indirect taxes (gabelle, traites, aides) in exchange for an advance lump-sum payment. This system, a source of immense fortunes but also of intense unpopularity, ended with the French Revolution — several fermiers généraux, including Lavoisier, were guillotined in 1794.

ferrailleur.label: Ferrailleur (scrap dealer)
ferrailleur.summary: Merchant and salvager of scrap metal, buying and reselling used metal objects and debris.
ferrailleur.text: The ferrailleur collects, sorts and resells scrap — worn-out iron or steel objects and debris — to supply foundries and forges with recycled raw material. This itinerant or fixed trade, often associated with ragpickers, is an old form of metal recycling.

ferrandinier.label: Ferrandinier
ferrandinier.summary: Weaver making ferrandine, a fabric mixing silk and wool (or thread), woven notably in Lyon.
ferrandinier.text: The ferrandinier weaves ferrandine, a light fabric mixing a silk warp with a wool or thread weft, whose manufacture developed in Lyon in the 17th century under the impetus of a weaver named Ferrand. Less costly than pure silk, it enjoyed great popular success before declining in the face of competition from other mixed fabrics.

ferratier.label: Ferratier
ferratier.summary: Regional term for scrap dealer: merchant who salvages and resells iron and used metal objects.
ferratier.text: The ferratier is a regional variant of the scrap dealer, denoting one who collects and resells scrap and old iron objects for reuse or remelting. The word is also attested as the name of a farrier's tool, reflecting the closeness between working iron and its salvage trade.

ferreur.label: Ferreur
ferreur.summary: Synonym for hemp-beater: worker who breaks hemp stalks with a flail or brake.
ferreur.text: The ferreur, a regional term equivalent to "batteur de chanvre" or "chanvrier", works to separate hemp's textile fibre from the woody part of the stalk (the "chènevotte"), using iron tools — hence the name — such as the brake or flail. This step follows the retting of the stalks and precedes the combing of the tow.

ferreur_d_aiguillettes.label: Ferreur d'aiguillettes
ferreur_d_aiguillettes.summary: Craftsman who fits the metal tip (the "fer") onto the end of aiguillettes, clothing cords.
ferreur_d_aiguillettes.text: The ferreur d'aiguillettes fixes a small metal tip (iron, brass or tin) to the end of aiguillettes — laces or cords used to fasten certain garment pieces before the button became widespread — to ease their passing through eyelets and prevent fraying. "Esguillettes" is the old spelling of "aiguillettes".

ferreur_de_formes.label: Ferreur de formes
ferreur_de_formes.summary: Shoemaking worker who nails and firmly fixes the sole to the shoe last.
ferreur_de_formes.text: The ferreur de formes takes part in shoemaking: he fixes the sole to the last (the wooden mould that gives the shoe its shape) using small nails, a step decisive for the shoe's sturdiness and comfort before industrial stitching or gluing developed.

ferrier.label: Ferrier
ferrier.summary: Iron worker, a generic term denoting one who works metal in a forge or an iron mine.
ferrier.text: "Ferrier" broadly denotes an iron worker, whether a blacksmith, an iron miner or a foundry worker depending on region and period. The term, vaguer than "forgeron" or "maréchal-ferrant", appears notably in old records of mining and iron-working regions.

ferron.label: Ferron
ferron.summary: Old term for a blacksmith or iron merchant, the origin of the surname Ferron.
ferron.text: "Ferron" is an old French word for a blacksmith or iron worker, now vanished from everyday use but fossilized in the surname Ferron, very common in western France. It shares its Latin root ("ferrum", iron) with "ferronnier" and "ferrailleur".

ferronnier.label: Ferronnier
ferronnier.summary: Craftsman who shapes wrought iron into utilitarian or decorative objects: railings, banisters, signs.
ferronnier.text: The ferronnier works iron with hammer and anvil to produce railings, balconies, staircase banisters, signs or art objects, in a tradition that distinguishes his decorative work from that of the more functional blacksmith or farrier. Art ironwork enjoyed a golden age in the Art Nouveau period, with figures such as Hector Guimard.

ferrotier.label: Ferrotier
ferrotier.summary: Glassworker responsible for gathering molten glass on the end of an iron rod to give it to the blower.
ferrotier.text: The ferrotier works within a glassworks team: using a "ferret", an iron rod, he gathers a mass of molten glass (the parison) from the furnace, which he then hands to the blower responsible for shaping it. This supporting trade, now vanished with the mechanization of the glass industry, illustrates the highly specialized organization of work in old glassworks.

ferteur.label: Ferteur
ferteur.summary: Textile worker who combs fibres (hemp or flax) to disentangle and align them before spinning.
ferteur.text: The ferteur combs hemp or flax tow using a hackle (a board bristling with iron points) to disentangle the fibres, remove impurities and align the strands for spinning. This step, between breaking and spinning proper, determines the fineness of the resulting thread.

feseresse_de_chapeaux_d_orfroi.label: Feseresse de chapeaux d'orfroi
feseresse_de_chapeaux_d_orfroi.summary: Luxury hat-maker embroidering orfroi (gold-thread) headwear for an aristocratic clientele.
feseresse_de_chapeaux_d_orfroi.text: The feseresse de chapeaux d'orfroi makes headwear adorned with orfroi embroidery — bands of fabric embroidered with gold or silver thread, also used on liturgical vestments — intended for a wealthy clientele. The term "orfroi" comes from the Latin "aurum phrygium", "gold of Phrygia", a region renowned in antiquity for its gold embroidery.

fesseresse_d_aumoniere_sarrazinoise.label: Fesseresse d'aumonière sarrazinoise
fesseresse_d_aumoniere_sarrazinoise.summary: Maker of richly adorned purses or bags.
fesseresse_d_aumoniere_sarrazinoise.text: The fesseresse d'aumônière sarrazinoise makes richly adorned purses or bags, called "à la sarrazinoise", a medieval term from Étienne Boileau's Book of Trades.

feuillagiste.label: Feuillagiste
feuillagiste.summary: Person who makes artificial flowers and foliage.
feuillagiste.text: The feuillagiste makes artificial flowers and foliage, a craft close to that of the florist-plumassier.

feuillardier.label: Hoop-wood cutter (feuillardier)
feuillardier.summary: Forest craftsman who shapes wooden circles from chestnut wood (hoop-wood) intended for cask binding.
feuillardier.text: The feuillardier exploits chestnut coppices — especially in Charente, Limousin, and northern Dordogne — to produce hoop-wood: stems split then bent into circles, used by the cooper to bind barrels and baskets. The term appeared only around 1850, though the trade is older; the number of feuillardiers, which reached 1,280 in 1906, later declined with competition from iron hoop-wood.

feutier.label: Felt maker (feutier)
feutier.summary: Maker of felt, a non-woven fabric obtained by fulling and pressing wool or hair fibres.
feutier.text: The feutier produces felt by fulling and pressing damp wool or animal-hair fibres (often rabbit or beaver hair) without passing through weaving. This material served notably in hat-making, which sometimes made this trade overlap with that of the felt-hat maker.

fevre_marechal.label: Smith-farrier (fèvre maréchal)
fevre_marechal.summary: Craftsman combining the skills of blacksmith and farrier, serving a rural community.
fevre_marechal.text: The fèvre-maréchal combined general iron work — tools, fittings, various repairs — with farrier work shoeing horses, two activities often distinct in towns but merged in small rural communities where a single craftsman had to answer all metallurgical needs. "Fèvre" comes from Latin faber, craftsman.

fiaker.label: Hackney coachman (Fiaker)
fiaker.summary: Driver of a two-horse hired carriage in Vienna; also the name of the carriage itself.
fiaker.text: The Fiaker drives a licensed two-horse hired carriage in Vienna, carrying passengers for payment; the name, borrowed from the Parisian "fiacre", denotes both the carriage and the coachman. Fiaker existed in Vienna from the late 17th century; they formed a well-known occupational group with customs of their own and still survive today as tourist carriages.

fidelier.label: Pasta maker (fidelier)
fidelier.summary: Provençal craftsman who produces food pasta, particularly fidéou (fine vermicelli), from durum wheat.
fidelier.text: The fidelier makes food pasta, particularly fidéou or fidés — fine vermicelli — typical of Provençal and more broadly Mediterranean cuisine (the word fideos is found in Catalan and Spanish). This artisanal activity, ancestor of industrial pasta factories, allowed long-term wheat preservation when transformed.

fiel_de_fechos.label: Fiel de fechos (Spanish village clerk)
fiel_de_fechos.summary: In Spanish villages without a notary, a resident authorised to act as council secretary and certify its acts.
fiel_de_fechos.text: In small communities that had no escribano, the fiel de fechos was the person authorised to write up the council's minutes, certify its decisions and keep the municipal papers. The post was often held by the schoolmaster or another resident who could read and write.

fifre.label: Fifer (fifre)
fifre.summary: Musician playing the fife, a small shrill flute used for military and naval signals and ceremonies.
fifre.text: The fifer is a musician who plays the fife, a small high-pitched wind instrument, employed aboard ships and in regiments to pace marching, transmit signals or animate ceremonies, often in a pair with a drummer. The role remained attested in sailing navies into the 19th century.

figurinaio.label: Figurinaio (plaster figure maker and pedlar)
figurinaio.summary: Maker and itinerant seller of plaster figurines, mostly from the Lucca area.
figurinaio.text: The figurinai, mainly from the Serchio valley and the province of Lucca, cast plaster figurines (saints, busts, animals) and sold them while travelling across Europe and the Americas, often organised in companies led by a master. The trade fed a significant migration flow between the 18th and 20th centuries.

figuriniste.label: Figurine maker (figuriniste)
figuriniste.summary: Creator of figurines or miniature costumes, for theatre, cinema or decorative sculpture.
figuriniste.text: The figuriniste (or figuriste) designs and creates figurines — small sculptures representing characters or scenes — or designs costume designs for spectacles, depending on context. The term covers both ancient art craftsmanship (nativity-figure maker, religious-figure sculptor) and contemporary theatre craft.

filandiere.label: Hemp/linen spinner (filandière)
filandiere.summary: Spinner specialized in spinning linen or hemp, a term also at the origin of the expression 'spider-spinner.'
filandiere.text: The filandière spins linen or hemp tow with a spindle or spinning wheel, work traditionally female and often practised at home to supplement agricultural income. The word also gave rise to the expression "araignée filandière" (spinner spider), naming certain web-spinning spiders, by analogy with the thread produced. "Filandier" is its masculine form, rarer.

filassier.label: Flax/hemp preparer (filassier)
filassier.summary: Textile worker who prepares flax (linen or hemp fibre) by breaking then combing, before spinning.
filassier.text: The filassier transforms retting-treated linen or hemp stems into flax (fibre): he breaks them to separate the textile fibre from the woody part, then combs it with a hackle to untangle and align the strands. The feminine "filassière" denoted more specifically the workers responsible for fine combing, the step following before spinning proper.

filateur.label: Spinning-mill owner (filateur)
filateur.summary: Industrialist directing a spinning mill, factory for transforming textile fibres into thread.
filateur.text: The filateur owns or directs a spinning mill, an industrial establishment equipped with spinning machines (mechanized from the late 18th century onward) transforming cotton, wool or linen into thread. The term thus designates rather an industrial entrepreneur than a simple spinner worker.

filatier.label: Sayette-thread merchant (filatier)
filatier.summary: Amiens merchant who sells sayette thread, supplying sayette weavers with fibre.
filatier.text: The filatier commercializes sayette thread — worsted wool thread mixed with a silk thread — used in sayette-making, a textile industry that developed in Amiens from the 16th century onward thanks to the arrival of reformed artisans. He often distributed carded wool to home spinners before collecting and reselling the thread obtained.

filatrice.label: Silk thread-winder (filatrice)
filatrice.summary: Worker who unwinds thread from silk cocoons by immersion in hot water.
filatrice.text: The filatrice works in a silk-spinning mill: she plunges cocoons in hot water to soften the gum binding the fibres, then unwinds several strands simultaneously to form a continuous, regular silk thread. This trade, essentially female, supported the rise of sericulture in south-eastern France, notably around Lyon.

fileresse.label: Silk spinner (fileresse)
fileresse.summary: Worker spinner unwinding and spinning silk, named according to the spindle size employed.
fileresse.text: The fileresse is a worker spinner unwinding and spinning silk, her designation varying according to the spindle size she employed.

aliases: Silk thread spinner with large and small spindles
fileresse_de_soie_a_grands_et_petits_fus.label: Silk spinner with various spindle sizes (fileresse de soie à grands et petits fuseaux)
fileresse_de_soie_a_grands_et_petits_fus.summary: Silk spinner using different spindle sizes to produce silk threads of varying qualities.
fileresse_de_soie_a_grands_et_petits_fus.text: The silk spinner with various spindle sizes adapted her tool to the result sought: the large spindle gave a thicker thread for common uses, the small spindle a finer thread reserved for precious fabrics. "Fileresse" is an old feminine form of "fileur," now replaced by "fileuse."

filetier.label: Fishing-net maker (filetier)
filetier.summary: Craftsman making fishing nets, by knotting threads according to the mesh suited to each use.
filetier.text: The filetier knots and assembles threads (hemp, then cotton or nylon) to make fishing nets, whose mesh and size vary according to the species sought and the fishing technique employed. This know-how, long transmitted in fisherman families of Breton and Norman ports, has largely disappeared with industrialized net-making.

filetoupier.label: Hemp beater (filetoupier)
filetoupier.summary: Farm worker who beats hemp to separate seeds and prepare stems for retting.
filetoupier.text: The filetoupier participated in the first stages of hemp work: beating dried stems to detach seeds (hemp seed), before the stems themselves were retting in water to free the textile fibre. The word seems composed of "fil" (thread) and "étoupe" (coarse fibre residue of hemp or linen).

fileur.label: Rope spinner (fileur)
fileur.summary: Cordage worker who regularly supplies the rope-works with fibres, controlling thread tension and regularity.
fileur.text: The fileur works in a rope-works: he supplies fibres (most often hemp) to the spinning mechanism, ensuring regular supply to obtain cordage of constant cross-section.
