peigneur_de_chevaux.text: The "peigneur de chevaux" was a groom specialised in treating horses suffering from "crapaudine", a disease of the hoof. The term therefore refers to an empirical veterinary speciality rather than to textile work, despite the similar vocabulary shared with the other combers in this dictionary.

peigneur_de_filozelle.label: Peigneur de filozelle (floss-silk comber)
peigneur_de_filozelle.summary: Worker who carded filozelle, a silk of inferior quality.
peigneur_de_filozelle.text: The "peigneur de filozelle" carded filozelle (floss silk), an inferior silk waste obtained from the residues of reeling, to prepare it for spinning. The trade belongs to the silk industries of the silk-producing regions.

peigneur_de_sayette.label: Peigneur de sayette (sayette comber)
peigneur_de_sayette.summary: Comber specialised in preparing sayette, a light fabric mixing wool and silk.
peigneur_de_sayette.text: The "peigneur de sayette" prepared sayette, a light fabric mixing wool and silk, by disentangling and aligning its fibres before spinning. This specialised textile trade is found in regions producing sayette goods, particularly in northern France.

peignier.label: Peignier (comb maker)
peignier.summary: Maker of combs in horn, bone or other materials.
peignier.text: The comb maker made combs, traditionally from cattle horn but also from bone, boxwood or tortoiseshell depending on region and period. The trade involved many successive specialisations along the production chain (planer, beader, sander, polisher), each corresponding to a distinct stage of shaping.

peintre.label: Peintre (painter)
peintre.summary: Craftsman or artist who painted pictures and decorations, or statues and religious images.
peintre.text: The painter practised a trade whose applications varied widely according to the period: in the Middle Ages and under the Ancien Régime, he often painted and gilded statues, altarpieces and images of saints for churches, within the framework of a regulated guild. The term covers both the craftsman-decorator and the recognised artist, the two figures being clearly distinguished only from the 17th and 18th centuries with the rise of the academies.

peintre_en_equipages.label: Peintre en équipages (coach painter)
peintre_en_equipages.summary: Painter specialised in decorating horse-drawn vehicles and coaches.
peintre_en_equipages.text: The coach painter adorned and decorated horse-drawn vehicles — coaches, calashes, berlins — painting coats of arms, lining and motifs on the body. This luxury trade accompanied the development of coachbuilding in the 18th and 19th centuries.

peintre_en_stores.label: Peintre en stores (blind painter)
peintre_en_stores.summary: Painter specialised in decorating fabric or wooden-slat blinds.
peintre_en_stores.text: The "peintre en stores" decorated blinds, whether of canvas or wooden slats, an item of interior furnishing that became widespread in the 19th century. The trade illustrates the growing specialisation of the decorative painting trades at that time.

peintre_sellier.label: Peintre sellier (saddle painter)
peintre_sellier.summary: Decorative painter specialised in ornamenting the leather of saddles.
peintre_sellier.text: The "peintre sellier" ornamented and decorated the leather of horse saddles, combining the work of the saddler with that of the decorative painter. The trade thus brought together two distinct craft skills in the service of equestrian equipment.

peleur_de_rotisses.label: Peleur de rôtisses (peeling labourer)
peleur_de_rotisses.summary: Day labourer who carried out peeling and preparation tasks.
peleur_de_rotisses.text: The "peleur de rôtisses" was a day labourer assigned to peeling and preparation tasks, probably connected with the barking of wood or with a poorly documented local craft. The rare term is found mainly in regional records.

pelhiere.label: Pelhière (rag and old-wool collector)
pelhiere.summary: Collector of used cloth and old woollens for textile recycling.
pelhiere.text: The "pelhière" collected used cloth and old woollens for recycling, notably for making rag paper or for reuse as textiles. "Peillarot" is a regional variant referring to the same activity.

pelletas.label: Pelletas (salt shoveller on a fishing boat)
pelletas.summary: Sailor responsible for shovelling salt into the hold of a fishing boat.
pelletas.text: The "pelletas" was a sailor responsible for shovelling salt into the hold of a fishing boat to preserve the fish during the campaign. The role was essential before artificial refrigeration became widespread for preserving catches at sea.

pelletier.label: Pelletier (furrier)
pelletier.summary: Furrier specialised in treating furs and making fur garments.
pelletier.text: The furrier worked and made up furs, preparing pelts to turn them into garments and trimmings. The trade, organised into a guild from the Middle Ages, is distinct from the "peaussier", who processed skins intended for leather rather than fur.

pellier.label: Pellier (hunter selling hides)
pellier.summary: Hunter of game who sold the skins to tanneries.
pellier.text: The "pellier" hunted game and sold the skins to tanneries to be turned into leather, forming a link between hunting and the leather crafts. The term is distinct from "pelletier", concerned with fine fur rather than raw hides.

pelonnier.label: Pelonnier (maker of wooden pegs)
pelonnier.summary: Woodworker who made joining and fastening pieces.
pelonnier.text: The "pelonnier" was a woodworker specialised in making small joining and fastening pieces, probably pegs or dowels. The term remains rare and poorly documented in genealogical sources.

pelotonneur.label: Pelotonneur (ball winder)
pelotonneur.summary: Spinning-mill worker who wound yarn into balls.
pelotonneur.text: The "pelotonneur" worked in a spinning mill, winding cotton, wool or other yarns into balls after spinning, ready for sale or later use in weaving. The trade accompanied the rise of the mechanised textile industry in the 19th century.

penichien.label: Pénichien (barge man)
penichien.summary: Boatman who operated barges for the river transport of goods.
penichien.text: The "pénichien" operated a barge ("péniche") used to carry goods on rivers and canals. The trade developed with the growth of the French canal network in the 19th and 20th centuries, offering an economical alternative to road and rail transport for heavy goods.

penon.label: Penon (foot messenger)
penon.summary: Messenger on foot carrying messages and letters.
penon.text: The "penon" was a messenger who travelled on foot to carry messages and letters, before the organisation of a structured postal service. The old term refers to a local communications role in the service of a community, a lord or an administration.

pensionnaire_militaire.label: Pensionnaire militaire (military pensioner)
pensionnaire_militaire.summary: Former serviceman receiving a State pension after his service.
pensionnaire_militaire.text: The military pensioner was a former soldier or retired officer receiving a pension paid by the State in recognition of his years of service, often after a wound or a discharge. The entry appears frequently in 19th-century civil registration records to describe former soldiers no longer in any occupation.

pepinieriste.label: Pépiniériste (nurseryman)
pepinieriste.summary: Grower who produced and sold young trees and shrubs.
pepinieriste.text: The nurseryman grew young plants — fruit trees, ornamental trees, vines — to be sold and then planted elsewhere. The trade became particularly professionalised from the 19th century onwards with the development of fruit growing and of large urban and forestry planting schemes.

perceur.label: Perceur (ship borer)
perceur.summary: Worker who bored, pinned and treenailed ships during their construction or refitting.
perceur.text: The "perceur" bored, pinned and treenailed ships in all their parts during their construction or refitting in a shipyard.

perceur_naval.label: Perceur naval (ship borer)
perceur_naval.summary: Shipyard worker specialised in boring and pinning ships.
perceur_naval.text: The "perceur naval" bored, pinned and treenailed ships' hulls in shipyards, preparing the timbers for assembly by specialised workers, upstream of the ship's carpenter. The trade formed part of the highly divided production chain of the Ancien Régime naval dockyards.

perceur_textile.label: Perceur, textile (Jacquard card puncher)
perceur_textile.summary: Worker who programmed Jacquard looms by punching cards.
perceur_textile.text: The textile "perceur" punched the cards used to program Jacquard looms, each hole determining the woven pattern. This invention of the early 19th century created a new workers' speciality, a distant forerunner of the punched-card programming later adopted in computing.

perforateur.label: Perforateur (card-punch operator)
perforateur.summary: 20th-century operator who punched cards for data entry.
perforateur.text: The card-punch operator ("perforateur" or "perforatrice") entered data by punching standardised cards, a process central to the punched-card and later computer processing of information in the 20th century, before keyboards and screens became widespread. It was often a job held by women in large public administrations and companies.

perfoverificateur.label: Perfovérificateur (punched-card verifier)
perfoverificateur.summary: Checker who verified the card punchers' work before computer processing.
perfoverificateur.text: The "perfovérificateur" checked the accuracy of the punched cards produced by the card-punch operators before they were processed by tabulating machines or the first computers. This 20th-century ancillary job disappeared as data-entry methods evolved.

perleur.label: Perleur (comb beader)
perleur.summary: Comb maker who hollowed out the base of the comb's large teeth.
perleur.text: The "perleur" was a comb-making worker responsible for hollowing out the base of the comb's large teeth, a stage of shaping that came after the planer (planeteur) and before the sander (ponceur). This very fine division of labour illustrates the guild organisation of the comb maker's trade.

perquilleur.label: Perquilleur (fish-weir fisherman)
perquilleur.summary: Coastal fisherman who worked a fish weir.
perquilleur.text: The "perquilleur" worked a fish weir, an enclosed area on the foreshore where fish were trapped by the falling tide, in order to catch them. This fixed fishing technique, practised on some coasts, did not require going out to sea.

perrayeux.label: Perrayeux (Anjou stone quarrier)
perrayeux.summary: Anjou worker who extracted the stone lying beneath the clay layers.
perrayeux.text: The "perrayeux" (or "perrayeur") was a worker from the Anjou region specialised in extracting the stone found beneath the clay layers. This regional quarrying trade is found mainly in records from Anjou.

perreyeur.label: Perreyeur (stone and slate worker)
perreyeur.summary: Worker who worked stone and slate, especially in quarries.
perreyeur.text: The "perreyeur" worked stone and slate, whether in a quarry or on site. The term has a great many spelling and regional variants — perreyeux, perrieur, perroyeur, pierroyeur — all referring to the same stonework, to be distinguished from the "perrier", more specifically associated with slate quarries.

perreyeur_cantonnier.label: Perreyeur cantonnier (waterway stonework maintenance man)
perreyeur_cantonnier.summary: Maintenance worker responsible for the stonework of a waterway.
perreyeur_cantonnier.text: The "perreyeur cantonnier" was a maintenance worker assigned to the upkeep of a waterway's stonework — banks, quays, locks. He combined the maintenance of river works with masonry skills.

perrier.label: Perrier (slate quarryman)
perrier.summary: Worker employed in working slate quarries.
perrier.text: The "perrier" worked at extracting slate in a quarry, a trade widespread in producing regions such as Anjou or the Ardennes. He differs from the "perreyeur" in his narrower specialisation in slate rather than stone in general.

perruquier.label: Perruquier (wigmaker)
perruquier.summary: Maker of wigs, often also a hairdresser and barber under the Ancien Régime.
perruquier.text: The wigmaker made wigs and frequently also worked as a hairdresser and barber, the three activities having long been grouped in a single guild under the Ancien Régime. The wearing of wigs, a symbol of social status from the 17th to the 18th century, gave the trade a well-to-do clientele before its decline after the Revolution.

perruquier_en_vieux.label: Perruquier en vieux (second-hand wig dealer)
perruquier_en_vieux.summary: Craftsman who exclusively repaired and resold second-hand wigs.
perruquier_en_vieux.text: The "perruquier en vieux" repaired and resold second-hand wigs, as distinct from the ordinary wigmaker, who made and sold new pieces. This specialisation reflects the internal hierarchy of the wigmakers' guild.

pesseleur.label: Pesseleur (vine-prop maker)
pesseleur.summary: Vineyard worker who planted and shaped the paisseaux (props) for vines.
pesseleur.text: The "pesseleur" shaped and planted "paisseaux", the wooden stakes supporting the vine stocks. "Paisseau" is a regional term attested by the CNRTL and Littré for the vine prop ("échalas"), used notably in Burgundy, the Lyonnais and the South-East. The trade accompanied the traditional staking of vines in these wine-growing regions.

petissier.label: Petissier (maker of wooden spoons)
petissier.summary: Craftsman who made spoons and small wooden table utensils.
petissier.text: The "petissier" made spoons and various small wooden table utensils, a craft close to that of the small-wares maker (tabletier) or the wood turner. The term remains rare and poorly attested in genealogical sources.

petrisseur.label: Pétrisseur (dough kneader)
petrisseur.summary: Baker's worker responsible for kneading bread dough.
petrisseur.text: The "pétrisseur" kneaded bread dough in bakehouses and bakeries, a physically demanding task before kneading was mechanised at the end of the 19th century. He generally worked under the authority of the master baker.

peyrolier.label: Peyrolier (maker of kitchen utensils, coppersmith)
peyrolier.summary: Maker of kitchen utensils in iron, copper, tin or lead.
peyrolier.text: The "peyrolier" made metal utensils for the kitchen and for crafts — cauldrons, saucepans, cooking pots — in iron, copper, tin or lead. The "peyroulier", an itinerant coppersmith who sold or repaired such utensils from village to village, is a variant.

pfleger.label: District governor (Pfleger)
pfleger.summary: Head of a Pfleggericht in Bavaria, Salzburg and Austria, both administrator and judge.
pfleger.text: The Pfleger heads a Pfleggericht, the ruler's lower administrative and judicial district in Bavaria, the Archbishopric of Salzburg and parts of Austria; he exercises police, lower and often higher jurisdiction, tax and military administration, frequently represented by a Pflegsverwalter or court clerk. The office lasted until the administrative reforms of the early 19th century. In records it must not be confused with the modern meaning of "Pfleger" (nurse or carer).

philosophe.label: Philosophe (philosophy-class pupil)
philosophe.summary: Pupil in the philosophy class, the final year of the Ancien Régime college curriculum.
philosophe.text: Under the Ancien Régime, the term "philosophe" in records often refers to a pupil in the philosophy class, the final year of the college curriculum, which covered logic, physics, metaphysics and ethics. It therefore does not necessarily mean a professional philosopher but a student status.

photographe.label: Photographe (photographer)
photographe.summary: Professional who took and developed photographs.
photographe.text: The photographer took pictures and developed them, a trade that appeared after the invention of photography in the 1830s and 1840s and quickly became professional with the rise of portrait studios in the 19th century. The term is commonly found in civil registration records from the late 19th century onwards.

phototypeur.label: Phototypeur (collotype printer)
phototypeur.summary: Printer who used collotype for postcards and labels.
phototypeur.text: The "phototypeur" printed by the collotype process ("phototypie"), a screenless photomechanical technique that reproduced images with great fineness of detail, used particularly for postcards and labels in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

physicien.label: Physicien (physician)
physicien.summary: Physician, in the old sense of the term.
physicien.text: In old usage, "physicien" refers to a physician, from the Latin "physica", which encompassed knowledge of the body and of nature. This sense, different from the modern meaning (a specialist in physics), is found in old records up to the 17th and 18th centuries.

picuriere.label: Picurière (seamstress)
picuriere.summary: Seamstress specialised in making and mending clothes.
picuriere.text: The "picurière" made and mended clothes, a sewing trade attested under many regional spelling variants — piquriere, piqurière, piqûriere — reflecting the variability of transcription in old records.

pierriste.label: Pierriste (gem and mineral specialist)
pierriste.summary: Collector of and specialist in precious and semi-precious stones and minerals.
pierriste.text: The "pierriste" studied, collected or dealt in precious and semi-precious stones and minerals. Depending on the context of the record, the term may refer to a dealer as much as to a learned amateur.

pieton_facteur.label: Piéton, poste (foot postman)
pieton_facteur.summary: Postal messenger who delivered mail on foot.
pieton_facteur.text: In the postal context, the "piéton" delivered mail on foot in towns and the countryside, before motorised rounds became widespread. The term remained in familiar use for the local postman until the 20th century.

pieton_soldat.label: Piéton, soldat (foot soldier)
pieton_soldat.summary: Infantry soldier fighting on foot, as opposed to the horseman.
pieton_soldat.text: In a military context, the "piéton" was an infantry soldier who fought on foot, as opposed to the mounted cavalryman. The term was used mainly in the 16th and 17th centuries, before "fantassin" became the dominant name.

pigionante.label: Pigionante (landless rural tenant)
pigionante.summary: In Tuscany, a landless rural worker who rented a house and lived by day labour.
pigionante.text: The pigionante, who paid rent (pigione) for a house or a few rooms in the countryside or a village, had no farm of his own and worked by the day for sharecroppers or estates, often supplementing this with small trades. In Tuscan parish censuses (stati delle anime) and population counts he appears as a category distinct from sharecroppers and landowners.

pile_tan.label: Pile-tan (tan-bark crusher)
pile_tan.summary: Worker who prepared tan (crushed bark) for tanneries.
pile_tan.text: The "pile-tan", a variant of the bark beater (batteur d'écorces), crushed and prepared tan, oak bark reduced to powder and used by tanners to tan hides. The trade was closely linked to the tanneries' activity.

pileur_de_laitier.label: Pileur de laitier (slag crusher)
pileur_de_laitier.text: The "pileur de laitier" crushed slag, the glassy residue from smelting ores in blast furnaces, so that it could be put to use (fill, ballast, road sub-base). The trade developed with the iron and steel industry of the 19th century.

pilhaouerien.label: Pilhaouerien (Breton rag pedlar)
pilhaouerien.summary: Breton itinerant rag dealer who exchanged goods for rags and rabbit skins.
pilhaouerien.text: The "pilhaouerien" (or "pilhaouaerien") was a Breton pedlar who exchanged manufactured articles — crockery, hardware, knick-knacks — for rags, rabbit skins, horsehair, pig bristles or scrap metal, which he then resold to wholesalers based in ports such as Morlaix; he also mended bowls, plates or umbrellas along his round. The word comes from the Breton "pilhoù" (rag). These pedlars were particularly numerous in the communes of the Monts d'Arrée (Botmeur, La Feuillée, Brennilis, Loqueffret).

pilonnier.label: Pilonnier (steam-hammer operator)
pilonnier.summary: Smith who worked the steam hammer in steelworks.
pilonnier.text: The "pilonnier" worked the power hammer ("marteau-pilon"), a percussion machine driven by steam and later by electricity, to forge and flatten large steel pieces. The trade developed with the industrialisation of iron and steel making in the 19th century.

pilote.label: Pilote (pilot)
pilote.summary: Navigator who guided ships through coastal and harbour approaches.
pilote.text: The pilot guided ships during the delicate manoeuvres of approaching coasts, harbours or channels, thanks to his detailed knowledge of the area. Piloting has been a regulated profession, often organised as a corporation in the ports, since the Ancien Régime.

pinceauteuse.label: Pinceauteuse (cloth retoucher)
pinceauteuse.summary: Woman worker who retouched painted cloths with a brush in a manufactory.
pinceauteuse.text: The "pinceauteuse" retouched painted or printed cloths with a brush in textile manufactories, a painstaking finishing task associated with the calico-printing works and printed-fabric factories of the 18th and 19th centuries.

pinier.label: Pinier (pine forester)
pinier.summary: Forester specialised in managing and exploiting pine trees.
pinier.text: The "pinier" managed and worked pine stands, notably for resin tapping ("gemmage") in the forests of the Landes, an activity that boomed from the 19th century onwards with the afforestation of the Landes de Gascogne.

pintier.label: Pintier (pewterer of measures)
pintier.summary: Pewterer who made measuring vessels such as the pinte.
pintier.text: The "pintier" was a pewterer specialised in making measuring vessels, including the "pinte", a unit of capacity common under the Ancien Régime. The trade belongs to pewter work.

pintor_de_azulejos.label: Pintor de azulejos (tile painter)
pintor_de_azulejos.summary: Craftsman who painted glazed tiles (azulejos) for wall coverings and decorative panels.
pintor_de_azulejos.text: The pintor de azulejos decorates, before firing, the glazed ceramic tiles used for wall coverings and figurative panels in churches, palaces, convents and on façades. The art flourished in Portugal, particularly in the 17th and 18th centuries with blue-and-white panels, and remained alive in the pottery and tile factories of the 19th and 20th centuries.

piocheur.label: Piocheur (railway navvy)
piocheur.summary: Railway worker responsible for building and maintaining railway lines.
piocheur.text: The "piocheur" worked on building and maintaining railway lines, digging and levelling the ballast with a pick. This earthworking trade accompanied the massive expansion of the French railway network in the 19th century.

piocheur_mineur.label: Piocheur-mineur (clay miner)
piocheur_mineur.summary: Worker who dug shafts and galleries to extract clay for potters.
piocheur_mineur.text: The "piocheur-mineur" dug shafts and galleries with a pick to extract clay for the pottery industry. The trade combined mining extraction techniques with a raw material used in crafts rather than heavy industry.

pioussaire.label: Pioussaïre (pioussaire)
pioussaire.text: Le pioussaïre tond les moutons en Provence, un métier saisonnier lié à l'élevage ovin traditionnel de la région. Le terme, occitan, désigne spécifiquement cette activité de tonte.

pipier.label: Pipier (pipe maker)
pipier.summary: Maker of pipes in wood, ivory or clay depending on the region.
pipier.text: The pipe maker made smoking pipes of clay, wood (notably briar from the 19th century onwards) or ivory, depending on the region and the materials available. The trade developed with the spread of smoking tobacco from the 17th century onwards.

piqueur.label: Piqueur (cod splitter)
piqueur.summary: Worker who prepared cod, cutting out the liver, entrails and head of the fish.
piqueur.text: In the cod fisheries, the "piqueur" cut up the cod to remove the liver, entrails and head, an essential step before the fish was salted and dried. The trade is found in the cod-fishing ports, especially those engaged in the Newfoundland fishery.

piqueur_conserverie.label: Piqueur, conserverie (cannery can piercer)
piqueur_conserverie.summary: Cannery worker who pierced metal cans.
piqueur_conserverie.text: The cannery "piqueur" pierced metal cans, a technical operation connected with the manufacture or testing of tins. The trade belonged to the emerging food-processing industry of the late 19th century.

piqueur_contremaitre.label: Piqueur, contremaître (timekeeping foreman)
piqueur_contremaitre.summary: Foreman who supervised workers and recorded absences on building sites.
piqueur_contremaitre.text: The "piqueur contremaître" supervised the workers on a site and recorded their attendance and absences, an intermediate supervisory role. The term "piqueur" here refers to the act of checking off, in the sense of marking or noting.

piqueur_d_escardes.label: Piqueur d'escardes (wool burler)
piqueur_d_escardes.summary: Textile worker who removed plant debris mixed in with wool.
piqueur_d_escardes.text: The "piqueur d'escardes" removed "escardes" — plant debris (thistles, twigs) caught in the fleece — before the wool was carded and spun. This preliminary cleaning was essential to the quality of the resulting yarn.

piqueur_de_cartons.label: Piqueur de cartons (Jacquard card puncher)
piqueur_de_cartons.summary: Textile worker who punched the cards used on Jacquard looms.
piqueur_de_cartons.text: The "piqueur de cartons" punched the cards that programmed the woven pattern on Jacquard looms, each punched card corresponding to one pick of the weft. The trade accompanied the spread of the Jacquard loom during the 19th century.

piqueur_de_gres.label: Piqueur de grès (sandstone dresser)
piqueur_de_gres.text: The "piqueur de grès" cut and shaped sandstone, a hard sedimentary rock used in building and paving. The trade is found in regions rich in sandstone quarries, such as the Île-de-France and the Vosges.

piqueur_de_meules.label: Piqueur de meules (millstone dresser)
piqueur_de_meules.summary: Craftsman who dressed and maintained millstones.
piqueur_de_meules.text: The millstone dresser cut the furrows of millstones and maintained their grinding surface, precision work indispensable to the proper running of grain mills. The trade declined with the mechanisation of milling at the end of the 19th century.

piqueur_de_pierres.label: Piqueur de pierres (stone dresser)
piqueur_de_pierres.summary: General stonecutter working different kinds of rock.
piqueur_de_pierres.text: The "piqueur de pierres" cut and shaped various rocks for building, a trade close to that of the stonecutter. The term emphasises the technique of "piquage", which consists in dressing the surface of the stone with hammer and chisel.

piqueur_de_sel.label: Piqueur de sel (rock-salt miner)
piqueur_de_sel.summary: Salt worker specialised in extracting rock salt.
piqueur_de_sel.text: The "piqueur de sel" extracted rock salt in a mine, breaking it away from the rock with striking tools. The trade is distinct from that of the "saunier" or the "paludier", who harvested sea salt by evaporation in salt marshes.

piqueur_dresseur_de_chevaux.label: Piqueur, dresseur de chevaux (riding master)
piqueur_dresseur_de_chevaux.summary: Master horseman specialised in haute école dressage.
piqueur_dresseur_de_chevaux.text: In this equestrian sense, the "piqueur" was a master horseman responsible for training horses according to the techniques of the haute école. The term was used particularly in the great royal and princely stables under the Ancien Régime.

piqueur_textile.label: Piqueur, textile (fabric stitcher)
piqueur_textile.summary: Textile worker responsible for stitching fabrics.
piqueur_textile.text: The textile "piqueur" stitched fabrics, a sewing or finishing operation depending on the type of cloth worked. The generic term covers several specific applications in the textile industry.

piqueuse_de_bottines.label: Piqueuse de bottines (boot closer)
piqueuse_de_bottines.summary: Woman shoe worker who did the decorative stitching of ankle boots.
piqueuse_de_bottines.text: The "piqueuse de bottines" stitched the uppers and did the decorative topstitching of ankle boots, a speciality of industrial shoemaking that developed with the mechanisation of footwear production at the end of the 19th century.

piqueux.label: Piqueux (huntsman)
piqueux.summary: Hunt servant in charge of the hounds and of handling the pack.
piqueux.text: The "piqueux" (or "piqueur") assisted the master of the hunt during hunts with hounds, directing the pack on horseback and sounding the horn to signal the progress of the chase. The trade still survives today in hunting establishments.

piquriere_2.label: Piqûrière (print-defect mender)
piquriere_2.summary: Woman worker who repaired defects found in the designs printed on pieces of cloth.
piquriere_2.text: The "piqûrière" repaired defects found in the patterns printed on pieces of cloth, painstaking retouching work specific to calico and printed-fabric manufactories. She is distinct from the "picurière", a seamstress making clothes, despite the similar names.

pisarz_gminny.label: Pisarz gminny (commune clerk)
pisarz_gminny.summary: Official running the office of a rural commune.
pisarz_gminny.text: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the pisarz gminny ran the office of a rural commune: correspondence, population registers, tax and conscription matters. He was often the only person in the commune skilled in official writing and played a considerable role alongside the wójt.

pisarz_miejski.label: Pisarz miejski (town clerk)
pisarz_miejski.summary: Official keeping the books and office of a town council.
pisarz_miejski.text: The pisarz miejski drew up and kept the books of the town council and bench of aldermen, and recorded deeds, contracts, wills and the town’s correspondence. He was expected to know Latin and municipal law well, and was one of the most important officials of town government.

pisarz_prowentowy.label: Pisarz prowentowy (estate clerk)
pisarz_prowentowy.summary: Manor-farm clerk keeping the accounts of the estate’s revenues.
pisarz_prowentowy.text: The pisarz prowentowy kept the books and accounts of a manor farm: income from crops, livestock and sales (prowenty), expenses and labour. It was often the first post of a young estate official, who could later be promoted to steward (ekonom) or administrator (rządca).

pizzaiolo.label: Pizzaiolo (pizza maker)
pizzaiolo.summary: Person who makes and bakes pizza.
pizzaiolo.text: The pizzaiolo prepares and bakes pizza in a wood-fired oven, following a tradition born in Naples, where in the 18th and 19th centuries pizzerias and street pizza sellers fed the working population. With emigration the trade spread throughout Italy and the world.

placeur.label: Placeur (usher)
placeur.summary: Employee who showed the public to their seats in theatres.
placeur.text: The "placeur", a variant of the usher (ouvreur), welcomed spectators and showed them to their seats in theatres and auditoriums. The job persisted into the modern age of cinema.

placier.label: Placier (market pitch allocator)
placier.summary: Person who allocated pitches to market traders and collected the fees for them.
placier.text: The "placier" allocated pitches to travelling traders at a market and collected the fees owed for their stalls.

placier_forain.label: Placier forain (market stallholder or pitch manager)
placier_forain.summary: Travelling trader who managed a pitch at markets and fairs.
placier_forain.text: The "placier forain" managed a selling pitch at markets and fairs, sometimes as the agent responsible for allocating pitches to itinerant traders. Depending on the case, the term covers either a trader or a market manager.

placier_representant.label: Placier, représentant (sales representative)
placier_representant.summary: Sales representative responsible for placing products with retailers.
placier_representant.text: In this commercial sense, the "placier" canvassed retailers to sell them a trading house's products, a role close to that of the modern sales representative or commercial traveller.

plafonneur.label: Plafonneur (plafonneur)
plafonneur.summary: Ouvrier réalisant et décorant les plafonds.
plafonneur.text: Le plafonneur réalise et décore les plafonds, en plâtre, en stuc ou peints, un métier proche du plâtrier mais spécialisé sur cet élément architectural précis.

plaggensteker.label: Plaggensteker (sod cutter)
plaggensteker.summary: Labourer who cut heath sods for bedding in the deep-litter byre.
plaggensteker.text: On the sandy soils of the eastern and southern Netherlands, heath and grass sods, called plaggen, were cut and used as bedding in the deep-litter byre. Mixed with dung, they were spread on the fields, which over the centuries raised the level of the arable land. Sod cutting was heavy work done by farmers and farmhands.

plancheieur.label: Planchéieur (floor layer)
plancheieur.summary: Worker who laid and fitted floors.
plancheieur.text: The "planchéieur" laid and fitted the wooden boards forming a building's floors, a finishing trade following the structural work, close to that of the joiner.

planeteur.label: Planeteur (comb planer)
planeteur.summary: Worker who planed and levelled surfaces, notably in comb making.
planeteur.text: The "planeteur" levelled and trued surfaces, in particular in the first stage of shaping comb teeth in the comb maker's workshop, before the beader (perleur) and then the sander (ponceur) took over. More broadly, the term refers to any planishing operation on metal or other material.

planeur.label: Planeur (planisher)
planeur.summary: Craftsman who levelled and smoothed surfaces, especially metal ones.
planeur.text: The "planeur" levelled and smoothed surfaces, in particular metal sheets or parts, to correct their distortions before final use. The term is found in several metal and wood trades.

platineur.label: Platineur (armour plate maker)
platineur.summary: Armourer responsible for making the small iron plates used in armour.
platineur.text: The "platineur" was an armourer's worker responsible for making the small iron plates ("carrelets") used in making armour.

platineur_armurier.label: Platineur armurier (armour plater)
platineur_armurier.summary: Armourer specialised in plating and finishing armour.
platineur_armurier.text: The "platineur armurier" carried out the plating and finishing of metal armour pieces, a specialisation of medieval and early modern armoury connected with the working of metal plates.

platineur_arquebusier.label: Platineur arquebusier (gunlock maker)
platineur_arquebusier.summary: Gunsmith's worker who made the firing mechanisms of firearms.
platineur_arquebusier.text: The "platineur arquebusier" made the lock ("platine"), the firing mechanism of portable firearms (flintlock, then percussion), a key and highly specialised part in the manufacture of early firearms.

platineur_de_faux.label: Platineur de faux (scythe-blade flattener)
platineur_de_faux.summary: Smith who flattened the steel for scythes and sickles under a power hammer.
platineur_de_faux.text: The "platineur de faux" forged and flattened, under a power hammer, the steel intended for scythes and sickles, a stage in the manufacture of these cutting farm tools, often carried out in specialised forges, notably in Auvergne.

platrier.label: Plâtrier (plasterer)
platrier.summary: Worker specialised in applying plaster coatings.
platrier.text: The plasterer applied plaster coatings to walls and ceilings, a building trade closely linked to that of the mason and sometimes confused with the ceiling plasterer (plafonneur). The spellings "platrier" and "plastrier" are old variants of the same word.

plieur.label: Plieur (cloth folder)
plieur.summary: Manufactory worker responsible for folding fabrics to standard sizes.
plieur.text: The "plieur" folded fabrics into standardised formats at the end of manufacture, a packaging operation carried out in textile manufactories before dispatch or sale.

plieur_de_fils.label: Plieur de fils (yarn folder)
plieur_de_fils.summary: Worker who prepared folded and tied skeins of yarn for weavers.
plieur_de_fils.text: The "plieur de fils" prepared folded and tied skeins of yarn for weavers, an intermediate stage in preparing the material before weaving proper.

plieur_de_livre.label: Plieur de livre (book folder)
plieur_de_livre.summary: Printing-works employee responsible for folding the pages of a book.
plieur_de_livre.text: The book folder folded the large printed sheets into gatherings in a precise order, a stage of book production in the printing works before binding. The job was long done by hand before folding was mechanised.

plieur_de_rouenneries.label: Plieur de rouenneries (warp preparer for rouenneries)
plieur_de_rouenneries.summary: Worker who prepared the warp of wool or silk yarn for weavers.
plieur_de_rouenneries.text: The "plieur de rouenneries" prepared the warp for the weavers of "rouenneries", printed cotton cloths originating from the Rouen area, a major textile centre in the 18th and 19th centuries.

plombeur.label: Plombeur (lead sealer)
plombeur.summary: Official who affixed lead seals certifying that duties and taxes had been paid.
plombeur.text: The plombeur affixed lead marks (seals, customs leads) to goods to certify that the required duties and taxes had been paid. This administrative occupation belonged to the tax and customs services of the Ancien Régime and the 19th century.

plombeur_marqueur.label: Plombeur (lead marker)
plombeur_marqueur.summary: Worker who marked objects with lead, a variant of the ferreur-marqueur.
plombeur_marqueur.text: The plombeur marqueur, a variant of the "ferreur et marqueur", affixed a lead mark to objects to certify that they conformed or had been inspected. The term is close to that of the fiscal plombeur, but applies to the marking of manufactured goods.

plombier.label: Plombier (plumber)
plombier.summary: Worker who handled lead and laid pipes in buildings.
plombier.text: The plombier worked lead, in particular for roofing and for laying water pipes, before the trade evolved into modern sanitary installation. The term has kept its original name even though lead largely gave way to other materials in the 20th century.

plommier.label: Plommier (lead-glazing potter)
plommier.summary: Earthenware potter who used "plommure" to glaze his pieces.
plommier.text: The plommier was an earthenware potter who used "plommure", a lead-based glaze, to make his pieces watertight and give them their characteristic glossy appearance. This glazing technique, common before the toxicity of lead was recognised, long characterised French folk pottery.

plumassiere.label: Plumassière (featherworker)
plumassiere.summary: Craftswoman who prepared and mounted ornamental feathers for fashion and costume.
plumassiere.text: The plumassière prepared, dyed and assembled feathers used to adorn hats, fans, stage costumes and ceremonial finery. The trade, organised as a guild in Paris (the "plumassiers-panachiers"), reached its height in the 18th and 19th centuries with the fashion for feathered hats, before declining in the 20th century with the protection of bird species and changing fashions.

plumet.label: Plumet (porter)
plumet.summary: Porter of goods in ports and carrier of grain in Paris.
plumet.text: The plumet carried goods in ports and transported grain in Paris, a handling job close to that of the "portefaix". Despite the resemblance of the word, the term refers to a labouring occupation rather than to any activity involving feathers.

podesta.label: Podestà (Italian chief magistrate)
podesta.summary: Magistrate at the head of an Italian commune; under Fascism, the government-appointed head of a municipality.
podesta.text: In the medieval Italian communes the podestà was a magistrate from another town, called in for a limited term to govern and administer justice above the factions. The title later designated the governors sent by Venice to the cities of its mainland and, in the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia, the head of some city administrations; from 1926 to 1945 the podestà, appointed by royal decree, replaced the mayor and the municipal council.

podestat.label: Podestat (noble judge of Soule)
podestat.summary: Nobleman of Soule who sat on the Cour du Noyer, one of the ten noble figures responsible for justice in Soule.
podestat.text: In Soule, a Basque province, the podestat (or potestat) was one of the ten noblemen obliged, in return for material advantages, to sit on the Cour du Noyer, the province's only civil and criminal court under the Ancien Régime, alongside the "capitaine-châtelain" and some fifty other landed noblemen. The term, of Italian origin ("podestà", a magistrate of the medieval communes), was adopted locally to designate this judicial and noble office peculiar to the institutions of Soule, which disappeared with the Revolution.

podlesniczy.label: Podleśniczy (assistant forester)
podlesniczy.summary: Assistant to a forester, overseeing part of a forest district.
podlesniczy.text: The podleśniczy helped the forester manage the forest, overseeing felling, planting and forest patrols in his assigned area. In the forest service hierarchy he ranked between the forester and the forest guard.

podstarosci.label: Podstarości (deputy starost)
podstarosci.summary: Deputy of a starost, managing a starosty or estates on his behalf.
podstarosci.text: The podstarości deputised for the starost in managing royal estates (a starosty) or in exercising the town-court jurisdiction. On large private estates the title also denoted the manager of a whole group of properties. Latin sources call him “vicecapitaneus”.

poelier.label: Poêlier (stove maker)
poelier.summary: Maker and seller of stoves and metal household goods.
poelier.text: The poêlier made and sold heating stoves and various metal household goods, a craft linked both to coppersmithing and to the trade in domestic utensils.

poete.label: Poète (poet)
poete.summary: Author who composed works in verse.
poete.text: The poet composed works in verse, an activity rarely practised as a profession in its own right before modern times and often mentioned alongside another occupation or social status. The term occasionally appears in records to describe a person recognised for this talent.

poffertjesbakker.label: Poffertjesbakker (poffertjes baker)
poffertjesbakker.summary: Baker who made poffertjes in a stall or tent at fairs and markets.
poffertjesbakker.text: The poffertjes baker cooked small fluffy pancakes in a cast-iron pan with many hollows, served with butter and icing sugar. The stalls, often richly decorated, travelled from fair to fair and were a fixture of Dutch popular entertainment.

poigneur.label: Poigneur (tailor)
poigneur.summary: Medieval name sometimes given to tailors.
poigneur.text: Poigneur is a medieval name sometimes given to tailors of clothing; the term remains rare and poorly attested in later genealogical sources.

poilier.label: Poilier (faience stove maker)
poilier.summary: Maker of faience stoves and other heating appliances.
poilier.text: The poilier made faience stoves and other domestic heating appliances, a craft close to that of the poêlier. The variants "poêlier-faïencier" and "poêlier-âtrier" specify this specialisation in making heating appliances in faience or ones installed at the hearth.

poinconneur.label: Poinçonneur (ticket puncher)
poinconneur.summary: Employee who punched transport tickets, notably in the Paris Métro.
poinconneur.text: The poinçonneur punched transport tickets with a pair of clippers, an iconic job in the Paris Métro throughout the 20th century, before automatic validation systems became widespread.

poissarde.label: Poissarde (fishwife)
poissarde.summary: Fish seller, the traditional name for the fishwives of Les Halles in Paris.
poissarde.text: The poissarde was a fish seller, a term long associated with the fishwives of Les Halles in Paris, who were known for their plain speaking, so much so that people spoke of the "style poissard" to describe this popular speech. The word is broadly synonymous with "poissonnière" but carries this cultural connotation specific to the common people of the Paris markets.

poissonnier.label: Poissonnier (fishmonger)
poissonnier.summary: Seller of freshwater or sea fish.
poissonnier.text: The poissonnier sold fish, freshwater or sea fish depending on his speciality and location, at markets or in a shop. The trade was closely tied to the supply networks for fresh fish, once constrained by transport times before refrigeration.

poldermolenaar.label: Poldermolenaar (drainage mill keeper)
poldermolenaar.summary: Miller who operated a drainage mill to pump water out of a polder.
poldermolenaar.text: The poldermolenaar lived with his family in or next to the mill and set it turning whenever the water level in the polder became too high, following the instructions of the water board. He maintained the sails, the scoop wheel or the Archimedean screw and was paid by the polder board. With the arrival of steam and later electric pumping stations the trade largely disappeared.

policier.label: Policier (police officer)
policier.summary: Officer responsible for upholding public order and the law.
policier.text: The policier is an officer responsible for upholding public order and ensuring the safety of people and property. The modern police, organised into professional forces, took shape gradually from the 19th century onwards, with the creation of municipal and then national forces.

polisseur_armurier.label: Polisseur (armourer's polisher)
polisseur_armurier.summary: Armourer's worker who polished the metal parts of weapons.
polisseur_armurier.text: The polisseur armurier polished the metal parts of weapons and armour, a finishing stage that gave them their shine and protected them against corrosion.

polisseur_de_peignes.label: Polisseur de peignes (comb polisher)
polisseur_de_peignes.summary: Comb maker who gave the comb its final touch of quality after the sander.
polisseur_de_peignes.text: The polisseur de peignes was a comb maker who, after the sander ("ponceur") had done his work, gave the comb its final touch of quality and finish.

polisseur_peignier.label: Polisseur (comb polisher)
polisseur_peignier.summary: Comb maker who gave the final touch of quality after the sander.
polisseur_peignier.text: The polisseur peignier gave the combs their final finishing touch after the work of the sander ("ponceur"), completing the highly divided production line of this trade ("planeteur", "perleur", "ponceur", "polisseur").

polisseuse.label: Polisseuse (jewellery polisher)
polisseuse.text: The polisseuse polished jewellery, traditionally using jeweller's rouge ("rouge d'Angleterre", iron oxide), to give it its final shine. This finishing trade was found in jewellers' and goldsmiths' workshops.

polletais.label: Polletais (Pollet fisherman)
polletais.summary: Fisherman from Dieppe specialising in Norman coastal fishing.
polletais.text: The polletais was a fisherman from the Pollet quarter of Dieppe, in Normandy, specialising in coastal fishing. The term refers to the inhabitants of this historic quarter of sailors and fishermen.

polrolnik.label: Półrolnik (half-holding peasant)
polrolnik.summary: Peasant farming half of a full peasant holding in old Poland.
polrolnik.text: The półrolnik (also półkmieć) worked roughly half of a kmieć’s holding and owed a correspondingly smaller share of labour service and dues. He formed an intermediate layer between the kmieć and the zagrodnik; Latin registers sometimes call him “semicmetho”.

pompier.label: Pompier (firefighter)
pompier.summary: Man responsible for fighting fires and maintaining firefighting equipment.
pompier.text: The pompier fought fires and maintained the equipment needed for the task (pumps, buckets, ladders). Fire brigades ("sapeurs-pompiers") were organised in France from the early 19th century, first in Paris as a battalion, then in the municipalities as volunteer corps, often made up of men who also had another trade.

pompiere_couture.label: Pompière (jacket alterations seamstress)
pompiere_couture.text: The pompière was a seamstress specialising in altering jackets, a speciality distinct from that of the "culottière" (trouser alterations) or the embroiderer within the garment trade. The term, attested in the vocabulary of dressmaking since the 19th century, is thought to refer to work done "à la pompe" in tailors' shops.

pompiste.label: Pompiste (petrol pump attendant)
pompiste.summary: Filling station employee who served petrol to motorists.
pompiste.text: The pompiste served petrol to motorists at a filling station, a job that appeared as cars became widespread in the 20th century and was gradually reduced by the spread of self-service from the 1970s and 1980s.

ponceur.label: Ponceur (comb sander)
ponceur.summary: Comb maker who removed grinding marks after the "perleur".
ponceur.text: The ponceur removed the grinding marks left on the comb after the work of the "perleur", before the final intervention of the polisher. This stage was part of the highly divided production line of comb making.

pontier.label: Pontier (bridge operator)
pontier.summary: Operator who worked swing bridges and movable bridges.
pontier.text: The pontier operated swing or movable bridges, allowing boats to pass along a canal or navigable river. This technical job accompanied the development of improved waterways in the 19th and 20th centuries.

pontonier.label: Pontonier (bridge or ferry keeper)
pontonier.summary: Person in charge of running a bridge or ferry, notably collecting the tolls.
pontonier.text: The pontonier was in charge of running a bridge or ferry, looking after its upkeep and often collecting the tolls owed by its users. The term is distinct from "pontonnier", a soldier of the military engineers responsible for building pontoon bridges.

pontonier_perception.label: Pontonier (toll collector)
pontonier_perception.summary: Official responsible for collecting tolls on bridges and ferries.
pontonier_perception.text: The pontonier de perception was specifically responsible for collecting the tolls on a bridge or ferry, a local fiscal function distinct from the physical upkeep of the structure.

pontonier_transbordeur.label: Pontonier (transporter bridge operator)
pontonier_transbordeur.summary: Employee of a transporter bridge responsible for its operation and for collecting tolls.
pontonier_transbordeur.text: The pontonier of a transporter bridge, a type of suspended movable bridge that carried passengers and vehicles from one bank to the other, operated the gondola and collected the toll. These bridges, built mainly between 1890 and 1920, remain rare and iconic.

pontonnier.label: Pontonnier (pontoneer)
pontonnier.summary: Soldier of the military engineers specialising in bridge building.
pontonnier.text: The pontonnier was a soldier of the military engineers specialising in bridge building, in particular pontoon bridges that allowed an army to cross a watercourse quickly. The corps of pontoneers formed a distinct technical arm within the engineers.

poppenkastspeler.label: Poppenkastspeler (Punch and Judy showman)
poppenkastspeler.summary: Travelling performer who gave glove-puppet shows in a puppet booth.
poppenkastspeler.text: The puppeteer travelled with his booth to markets, fairs and streets and performed short plays with glove puppets around fixed characters, in the Netherlands mainly Jan Klaassen and Katrijn. He earned his income by collecting money from the audience.

porcelainier.label: Porcelainier (porcelain maker)
porcelainier.summary: Worker specialising in making and decorating porcelain.
porcelainier.text: The porcelainier made and decorated porcelain pieces, a luxury craft that developed in France from the 18th century with the rise of manufactories such as those of Sèvres and Limoges.

porchard.label: Porchard (gelder)
porchard.summary: Regional term for a gelder who castrated small domestic animals.
porchard.text: In the dialect of the Brionnais and the Charolais, the porchard was a gelder specialising in the castration of small domestic animals. "Portsale" is the equivalent regional name for the same activity.

porcher.label: Porcher (swineherd)
porcher.text: The porcher bred and kept pigs, a pastoral occupation common in the French countryside, the herd often being taken to graze in the forest (pannage, "glandée") to feed on acorns and beechnuts.

porgeur.label: Porgeur (drawer-in)
porgeur.summary: Textile worker who threaded the warp yarns through the heddles of the loom.
porgeur.text: The porgeur threaded the warp yarns through the heddles of the loom, a painstaking preparatory operation essential before the weaving itself could begin.

porion.label: Porion (mine overman)
porion.summary: Mining foreman in charge of a working face or a gallery.
porion.text: The porion was the foreman who ran a working face or gallery in a coal mine, supervising the miners under the authority of the engineer. The term, widely used in the coalfields of Nord-Pas-de-Calais, refers to a central figure in the organisation of mining work.

porion_de_trait.label: Porion de trait (haulage overman)
porion_de_trait.summary: Porion specialising in supervising the haulage of ore.
porion_de_trait.text: The porion de trait specifically supervised the haulage of coal or ore underground, a specialisation of the porion within the organisation of the mine.

portageur.label: Portageur (packer)
portageur.summary: Canadian porter who carried food and tools to lumberjacks in the forest.
portageur.text: The portageur carried food and tools to the lumberjack crews in the logging camps, an occupation characteristic of French-Canadian forestry. The term is also used for crossing an obstacle on a river on foot while carrying a boat or a load.

porte_a_dos.label: Porte à dos (backpack smuggler)
porte_a_dos.summary: Smuggler who carried prohibited goods on his back.
porte_a_dos.text: The porte à dos carried prohibited goods on his back across border areas or mountain passes, thereby escaping customs surveillance. The term is found in particular in the smuggling regions of the Pyrenees and the Alps.

porte_clefs.label: Porte-clefs (turnkey)
porte_clefs.summary: Prison warder responsible for the keys and for watching over the prisoners.
porte_clefs.text: The porte-clefs was a prison warder responsible for holding the cell keys and keeping daily watch over the prisoners, a subordinate but essential function in the prison administration of the Ancien Régime and the 19th century.

porte_coton_marine.label: Porte coton (naval officer's attendant)
porte_coton_marine.summary: Naval cadet assigned to the personal service of a senior officer.
porte_coton_marine.text: In the navy, the porte coton was a young cadet assigned to the personal service of a senior officer, a subordinate apprentice role within the naval hierarchy.

porte_coton_royal.label: Porte coton (royal attendant)
porte_coton_royal.summary: Honorary office of attending the king in his intimate needs.
porte_coton_royal.text: The royal porte coton held an honorary office in the king's household that consisted of attending him in his intimate needs, illustrating the meticulous hierarchy of domestic offices at court under the Ancien Régime.

porte_manteau.label: Porte-manteau (cloak bearer)
porte_manteau.summary: Officer responsible for carrying the cloak of members of the royal family.
porte_manteau.text: The porte-manteau was an officer of the royal or princely household responsible for carrying his master's ceremonial cloak, an honorary court office.

porte_sacs.label: Porte sacs (mail-bag carrier)
porte_sacs.summary: 18th-century postman who carried mail in Paris.
porte_sacs.text: In the 18th century, the porte sacs carried the mail bags in Paris, a function that foreshadowed that of the postman before the modern organisation of postal delivery.

porte_sonnette.label: Porte-sonnette (bell ringer)
porte_sonnette.summary: Municipal employee who rang a bell to announce the time of street cleaning.
porte_sonnette.text: The porte-sonnette was a municipal employee who, by ringing a handbell in the streets, told the inhabitants when the cleaning or collection would take place, a function attested notably in Brive. He is distinguished from ordinary town criers by his specific use of the bell as a signal.

portefaix.label: Portefaix (porter)
portefaix.summary: Porter specialising in loading and unloading goods.
portefaix.text: The portefaix loaded and unloaded goods, particularly in ports, market halls and warehouses, carrying them on his back or in a pannier. This labouring occupation, very widespread before the mechanisation of handling, was often organised as a guild in the large port cities.

porteresse.label: Porteresse (salt carrier)
porteresse.summary: Woman who carried the harvested salt from the marshes to the storage sites.
porteresse.text: The porteresse carried the salt harvested in the salt marshes to the storage sites, a traditionally female task in salt-producing regions such as the Vendée and Brittany.

porteur.label: Porteur (sedan-chair bearer)
porteur.summary: Bearer who carried people in a sedan chair.
porteur.text: The porteur carried seated passengers in a sedan chair, a means of individual urban transport widely used in the 17th and 18th centuries before the spread of the hackney cab and then the motor car. The job was often done in pairs, the two bearers sharing the poles.

porteur_a_l_arche.label: Porteur à l'arche (glassworks lehr attendant)
porteur_a_l_arche.summary: Glassworks employee responsible for counting and checking the quality of the pieces.
porteur_a_l_arche.text: The porteur à l'arche counted and checked the quality of the glass pieces as they came out of the kiln known as the "arche de recuisson" (annealing oven), where the glass cooled gradually to prevent it from cracking. This post was part of the highly hierarchical production line of Ancien Régime glassworks.

porteur_d_argent.label: Porteur d'argent (money carrier)
porteur_d_argent.text: The porteur d'argent transported funds safely on behalf of an administration, a bank or a private individual, a position of trust that foreshadowed the modern security van guard.

porteur_d_eau.label: Porteur d'eau (water carrier)
porteur_d_eau.summary: Man who carried water from the fountains to private homes.
porteur_d_eau.text: The porteur d'eau carried water from fountains, pumps or streams to private homes, before running water became widespread.

porteur_de_contraintes.label: Porteur de contraintes (tax summons server)
porteur_de_contraintes.summary: Official who served formal tax demands on taxpayers.
porteur_de_contraintes.text: The porteur de contraintes served taxpayers with the writs of distraint ("contraintes", formal demands) issued for the collection of taxes, an administrative function linked to the tax system of the Ancien Régime and the 19th century.

porteur_de_garantie.label: Porteur de garantie (assay office carrier)
porteur_de_garantie.summary: Clerk who carried precious objects to the hallmarking office.
porteur_de_garantie.text: The porteur de garantie carried pieces of gold and silver work to the assay office ("bureau de garantie"), where they received the official hallmark certifying the fineness of the precious metal. This function was part of the regulated system for controlling precious metals.

porteur_de_glace.label: Porteur de glace (ice carrier)
porteur_de_glace.summary: Carrier of blocks of natural ice to spa towns.
porteur_de_glace.text: The porteur de glace carried blocks of natural ice, harvested in winter and kept in an ice house, to spa towns or shops, before the production of artificial ice became widespread at the end of the 19th century.

porteur_de_greve.label: Porteur de grève (sand and gravel carrier)
porteur_de_greve.summary: Handler specialising in sand and gravel ports.
porteur_de_greve.text: The porteur de grève carried sand and gravel in river or sea ports, a handling job linked to the extraction of and trade in building materials.

porteur_de_guy.label: Porteur de guy (haulers' leader)
porteur_de_guy.summary: Hauler in charge of a coordinated towing team on the river.
porteur_de_guy.text: The porteur de guy led a team of haulers who towed boats along the waterways with ropes, the "guy" being the rope or towing device. The job disappeared with the motorisation of river transport.

porteur_de_sel.label: Porteur de sel (salt porter)
porteur_de_sel.summary: Employee of the gabelle who carried salt from the ships to the salt stores.
porteur_de_sel.text: The porteur de sel carried salt from the ships or salt marshes to the salt stores ("greniers à sel"), within the highly regulated system of the gabelle (salt tax) under the Ancien Régime.

porteuse_de_bain.label: Porteuse de bain (bath-water carrier)
porteuse_de_bain.summary: Woman who delivered the hot water needed for baths at home.
porteuse_de_bain.text: The porteuse de bain delivered the hot water needed for baths taken at home, before running water and domestic heating became widespread. This urban occupation survived for a long time in the large cities.

portier.label: Portier (porter, doorkeeper)
portier.summary: Employee responsible for receiving visitors and watching over an entrance.
portier.text: The portier received visitors and watched over the entrance of an establishment, a residence or a convent. The term is found for a lay employee as well as for a member of a religious order given this task in a monastery.

portraitiste.label: Portraitiste (portraitist)
portraitiste.summary: Artist specialising in drawn or painted portraits.
portraitiste.text: The portraitiste made portraits that were drawn, painted or photographed depending on the period, an artistic genre particularly prized by bourgeois and aristocratic clients before photography became widely accessible.

poseur_de_jambe.label: Poseur de jambe (stem maker)
poseur_de_jambe.summary: Glassworker who formed the stem of stemmed glasses in a crystal works.
poseur_de_jambe.text: The poseur de jambe shaped the stem ("jambe") of stemmed glasses in a crystal works, a specialised stage in the making of hand-blown glass.

poseur_de_lignes.label: Poseur de lignes (platelayer)
poseur_de_lignes.summary: Worker who built and laid railway tracks.
poseur_de_lignes.text: The poseur de lignes built and laid railway tracks, assembling rails and sleepers on the ballast. This earthworks and construction job accompanied the expansion of the French railway network in the 19th century.

poseur_de_pied.label: Poseur de pied (foot maker)
poseur_de_pied.summary: Glassworker who formed the foot of glasses onto the stem in a crystal works.
poseur_de_pied.text: In a crystal works, the poseur de pied shaped the foot of drinking glasses onto the stem, completing the work of the "poseur de jambe" in the making of hand-blown glass.

posticheur.label: Posticheur (hairpiece maker)
posticheur.text: The posticheur made hairpieces and wigs, a craft of artificial hairdressing close to that of the wigmaker.

postillon.label: Postillon (postilion)
postillon.summary: Driver of a team of horses for the mounted postal service.
postillon.text: The postillon drove a team of horses, riding one of them, to provide the postal service and carry travellers from relay to relay before the coming of the railway. The occupation gradually disappeared from the middle of the 19th century.

potaignier.label: Potaignier (pewterer)
potaignier.summary: Pewterer from the Huy region in Belgium.
potaignier.text: The potaignier worked pewter in the region of Huy, in Belgium, a renowned centre of "potaigne" (pewter) since the Middle Ages. The term therefore refers to a regional pewterer rather than an earthenware potter.

potier.label: Potier (potter)
potier.summary: Maker of kitchen utensils and containers in various materials.
potier.text: The potier made kitchen utensils and various containers, traditionally in earthenware but also in pewter depending on the specialisation ("potier de terre", "potier d'étain"). This very ancient trade is found throughout France with strong regional traditions.

potier_d_etain.label: Potier d'étain (pewterer)
potier_d_etain.summary: Spelling variant designating the craftsman who worked pewter.
potier_d_etain.text: The potier d'étain (sometimes spelled "potier d'estaing") made utensils and containers in pewter, a metalworking trade distinct from that of the earthenware potter, who worked clay.

potier_de_terre.label: Potier de terre (earthenware potter)
potier_de_terre.summary: Potter who worked clay, as opposed to the pewterer.
potier_de_terre.text: The potier de terre worked clay to make earthenware utensils and containers, as opposed to the "potier d'étain", who worked metal. This is the most common meaning of the word "potier" in old records.

poudrier.label: Poudrier (powder maker)
poudrier.summary: Person in charge of the military powder magazine and explosives.
poudrier.text: The poudrier made or managed gunpowder and explosives, often within a royal or military powder works that was a state monopoly under the Ancien Régime.

poulailler.label: Poulailler (poulterer)
poulailler.summary: Poultry dealer who went round the farms.
poulailler.text: The poulailler was a poultry dealer who went round the farms buying hens, ducks and other poultry to sell them on at urban markets.

poulieur.label: Poulieur (block maker)
poulieur.summary: Maker of pulleys for mechanical equipment.
poulieur.text: The poulieur made pulleys for mechanical equipment, in particular for ships (rigging) or for industry, a craft working in wood and metal.

poupelier.label: Poupelier (fibre bundler)
poupelier.summary: Worker who made up textile fibres into bundles for sale.
poupelier.text: The poupelier made up textile fibres into skeins or "poupées" (packaged bundles) for sale, a packaging stage in the textile industry.

poupetier.label: Poupetier (doll seller)
poupetier.summary: Merchant specialising in the sale of dolls.
poupetier.text: The poupetier sold dolls, a toy trade that developed with the rise of the toy industry in the 19th century.

pouplassier.label: Pouplassier (tow and cord dealer)
pouplassier.summary: Dealer in tow and various textile cords.
pouplassier.text: The pouplassier traded in tow ("filasse"), the raw textile fibres of flax or hemp, and in cords, a trade linked to the textile industry and to ropemaking.

pourpointier.label: Pourpointier (doublet maker)
pourpointier.text: The pourpointier made doublets ("pourpoints"), the close-fitting men's garment covering the torso worn from the Middle Ages to the 17th century. The trade, organised as a guild, declined when this garment was abandoned in favour of other fashions.

pourvoyeur_de_fleurets.label: Pourvoyeur de fleurets (drill-steel boy)
pourvoyeur_de_fleurets.summary: Child who supplied the miners with specialised tools.
pourvoyeur_de_fleurets.text: The pourvoyeur de fleurets supplied the miners with drill steels ("fleurets"), the metal rods used for drilling, a task often given to young boys working underground before child labour in the mines was banned.

poussecul.label: Poussecul (bailiff's man)
poussecul.summary: Popular term for the "recors", bailiffs' assistants.
poussecul.text: Poussecul was a popular and pejorative term for the "recors", the assistants who accompanied bailiffs to lend them a hand during seizures and arrests.

poustier.label: Poustier (communal oven carrier)
poustier.summary: Employee of the communal oven who collected and returned the bread to be baked.
poustier.text: The poustier collected the loaves of dough from the inhabitants and brought them back baked from the "four banal", the lord's communal oven that villagers were obliged to use for a fee under the Ancien Régime.

pralat.label: Prałat (prelate)
pralat.summary: Senior cleric holding a church dignity, especially in a chapter.
pralat.text: The prałat is a cleric holding a senior dignity in a chapter (such as provost, dean, custodian or scholaster) or an honorary title granted by the pope. The title indicated a high position in the church hierarchy.

praticien.label: Praticien (law clerk)
praticien.summary: Young lawyer working as a clerk or trainee in a notary's office.
praticien.text: The praticien was a young lawyer working as a clerk or trainee in a notary's office, the first step in his training.

praticien_juriste.label: Praticien (legal practitioner)
praticien_juriste.summary: Young lawyer working as a clerk or trainee to a notary.
praticien_juriste.text: The praticien juriste was a young man of law who worked as a clerk or trainee, often in a notary's office, in order to complete his practical training before setting up on his own.

praticien_medecin.label: Praticien (médecin) (praticien_medecin)
praticien_medecin.text: Le praticien, dans le domaine médical, désigne un médecin exerçant effectivement son art auprès de patients, par opposition à un titre purement théorique ou honorifique.

praticien_notaire.label: Praticien (seigneurial notary)
praticien_notaire.summary: Seigneurial officer with legal knowledge but no degree.
praticien_notaire.text: The praticien notaire carried out seigneurial notarial functions thanks to his practical legal knowledge, without necessarily holding a university degree, a situation more frequent in the small rural jurisdictions of the Ancien Régime.

prebendier.label: Prébendier (prebendary)
prebendier.summary: Churchman holding a prebend, ranking below a canon.
prebendier.text: The prébendier was a churchman holding a prebend, an income attached to a cathedral or collegiate church, but ranking below a canon. This hierarchy of benefices structured the secular clergy under the Ancien Régime.

precepteur.label: Précepteur (private tutor)
precepteur.summary: Private educator who taught the children of well-off families.
precepteur.text: The précepteur provided private instruction to children within well-off families, a widespread practice among the nobility and the upper bourgeoisie before state schooling became general at the end of the 19th century.

premier_lieutenant_de_cavalerie.label: Premier-lieutenant de cavalerie (cavalry first lieutenant)
premier_lieutenant_de_cavalerie.summary: Junior officer commanding a cavalry unit.
premier_lieutenant_de_cavalerie.text: The premier-lieutenant de cavalerie was a junior officer of the cavalry arm, a rank between second lieutenant and captain in the military hierarchy of several French-speaking armies, including the Swiss army.

premier_peintre_du_roi.label: Premier peintre du roi (First Painter to the King)
premier_peintre_du_roi.summary: Artist who directed the royal artistic works.
premier_peintre_du_roi.text: The First Painter to the King directed the artistic works commissioned by the crown and often supervised the Royal Academy of Painting, a prestigious office held by renowned artists such as Charles Le Brun under Louis XIV.

prenditore_del_lotto.label: Prenditore del lotto (lottery office keeper)
prenditore_del_lotto.summary: Keeper of a lotto office who took the players' stakes.
prenditore_del_lotto.text: The prenditore del lotto ran, under a state licence, an office (the botteghino) where players placed their stakes on the lotto numbers, and paid out the winnings. The game, of Genoese origin, was run as a public monopoly by the pre-unification Italian states and then by the Kingdom of Italy.

preparateur_d_ecole.label: Préparateur d'école (laboratory technician)
preparateur_d_ecole.summary: Technical assistant who prepared scientific experiments.
preparateur_d_ecole.text: The préparateur d'école prepared the equipment and scientific experiments used in science lessons, a technical assistant's role that appeared with the development of science teaching in the "collèges" and "lycées".

prepose_au_sel.label: Préposé au sel (salt official)
prepose_au_sel.summary: Employee responsible for collecting and distributing salt under the royal tax.
prepose_au_sel.text: The préposé au sel collected and distributed salt under the gabelle, the royal salt tax that obliged subjects to buy their salt from the official salt store ("grenier à sel"). This administrative function disappeared with the abolition of the gabelle during the Revolution.

president_d_election.label: Président d'élection (president of an election court)
president_d_election.summary: Magistrate who presided over the court of an "élection", an Ancien Régime tax jurisdiction.
president_d_election.text: The président d'élection presided over the court of an "élection", an Ancien Régime tax district responsible in particular for disputes over the taille and other direct taxes. This jurisdiction disappeared with the administrative reform of the Revolution.

president_du_gouvernement_cantonal.label: Président du gouvernement cantonal (president of a cantonal government)
president_du_gouvernement_cantonal.summary: Head of the executive of a Swiss canton.
president_du_gouvernement_cantonal.text: The président du gouvernement cantonal chairs the executive council of a Swiss canton, the collegial body responsible for the cantonal administration. The exact title and the length of the term vary from canton to canton, the post often being held in rotation by the members of the council.

presseur.label: Presseur (cloth presser)
presseur.summary: Textile worker who used the press to finish fabrics.
presseur.text: The presseur used a press for the final dressing of fabrics, giving them lustre and firmness before they were put on sale, a finishing operation in the textile industry.

pressoirier.label: Pressoirier (wine-press operator)
pressoirier.summary: Worker specialising in operating the wine press.
pressoirier.text: The pressoirier operated the press to extract the juice from the harvested grapes, a seasonal job essential to the grape harvest. The term has several spelling variants: "pressorier", "pressureur", "pressurier".

prestidigitateur.label: Prestidigitateur (conjurer)
prestidigitateur.summary: Performer specialising in magic tricks and illusions.
prestidigitateur.text: The prestidigitateur entertained the public with magic tricks and illusions, mastering techniques of quick ("preste") sleight of hand. The occupation became professional especially in the 19th century with figures such as Robert-Houdin.

preteur_sur_gages.label: Prêteur sur gages (pawnbroker)
preteur_sur_gages.summary: Lender who advanced money against a pledge of valuables.
preteur_sur_gages.text: The prêteur sur gages advanced money in exchange for valuables deposited as security, which the borrower recovered on repaying the loan. This activity, often regulated or even taken over by public institutions such as the Mont-de-Piété from the 18th century, met the credit needs of the working classes.

pretore.label: Pretore (Italian district judge)
pretore.summary: Single judge of first instance with jurisdiction over a judicial district (mandamento) in Italy.
pretore.text: In the Kingdom of Italy the pretore tried minor civil cases and minor offences within a mandamento, a district grouping several municipalities, and also dealt with non-contentious matters (guardianships, successions). Successor to the district judges of the pre-unification states, the office lasted until the pretura courts were abolished at the end of the 20th century. The term also designates the praetor of ancient Rome.

aliases: Prêtre de la paroisse du prieuré
pretre.label: Prêtre (priest)
pretre.summary: Ordained churchman authorised to celebrate the Catholic sacraments.
pretre.text: The prêtre is an ordained churchman authorised to celebrate Mass and administer the sacraments. Under the Ancien Régime, parish priests and priests kept the parish registers (baptisms, marriages, burials), which then served as the civil registers; after civil registration was secularised in 1792, they continued to keep parallel religious registers. The entries "prêtre de la paroisse", "prêtre de la paroisse du prieuré" or "prêtre-vicaire" denote variants of function or attachment (incumbent parish priest, priest serving a priory, or priest assisting a parish priest), but all belong to the same ecclesiastical state.

preveneur_imperial.label: Procureur impérial (imperial prosecutor)
preveneur_imperial.summary: Title of the public prosecutor under the Second Empire.
preveneur_imperial.text: The procureur impérial was the title borne by the magistrate acting as public prosecutor at a court under the Second Empire (1852-1870), instead of the "procureur de la République" used under the republican regimes. The function remained identical to that of the ordinary prosecutor, only the name changing with the political regime.

prevot.label: Prévôt (provost)
prevot.summary: Head of certain cathedral and collegiate churches.
prevot.text: In the ecclesiastical sphere, the prévôt headed certain cathedral and collegiate churches, holding a chapter dignity. In other contexts the same word also refers to distinct judicial or military officers, presented separately in this dictionary.

prevot_d_equipage.label: Prévôt d'équipage (ship's provost)
prevot_d_equipage.summary: Naval officer who carried out corporal punishment on board ship.
prevot_d_equipage.text: On board ship, the prévôt d'équipage was responsible for carrying out the corporal punishments decided by maritime justice, a disciplinary function of the Ancien Régime navy.

prevot_de_l_armee.label: Prévôt de l'armée (army provost)
prevot_de_l_armee.summary: Officer responsible for maintaining order among the troops.
prevot_de_l_armee.text: The prévôt de l'armée was an officer in charge of maintaining order and military discipline among the troops, an old military police function that foreshadowed the provostship of the maréchaussée and then the gendarmerie.

prevot_de_l_hotel_du_roi.label: Prévôt de l'hôtel du roi (provost of the King's household)
prevot_de_l_hotel_du_roi.summary: Officer of the sword who judged all persons in the retinue of the Court.
prevot_de_l_hotel_du_roi.text: The prévôt de l'Hôtel du roi was an officer of the sword who judged all persons attached to the retinue of the royal Court.

prevot_de_la_marechaussee.label: Prévôt de la maréchaussée (provost of the mounted constabulary)
prevot_de_la_marechaussee.summary: Officer responsible for the safety of the highways, forerunner of the gendarmerie.
prevot_de_la_marechaussee.text: This provost was the officer in charge of the safety of the highways and of rural policing under the Ancien Régime, commanding a brigade of the maréchaussée. This institution, whose older title was "prévôt des maréchaux", was the direct origin of the national gendarmerie created in 1791.

prevot_de_la_marine.label: Prévôt de la marine (naval provost)
prevot_de_la_marine.summary: Senior officer of the naval archers.
prevot_de_la_marine.text: The naval provost commanded the naval archers ("archers de la marine"), a maritime police force responsible for maintaining order in the ports and naval dockyards under the Ancien Régime.

prevot_de_salle.label: Prévôt de salle (assistant fencing master)
prevot_de_salle.summary: Assistant to the fencing master who gave lessons to pupils.
prevot_de_salle.text: The prévôt de salle assisted the fencing master in a fencing hall, notably by giving lessons himself to beginners, an intermediate grade in the hierarchy of fencing instruction.
